nodes.title: Extensions of semistable representations that are de Rham are semistable; ordinary representations are semistable
nodes.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite. (a) If E is a de Rham representation of G_K which is an extension of W by V with V, W semistable, then E is semistable. (b) If V is de Rham with all Hodge–Tate weights ≥ 1 (HT(χ_p) = +1), then every extension of Q_p by V is de Rham: H^1(K, V) = H^1_g(K, V). (c) Every ordinary representation of G_K is semistable (in particular de Rham), and its Hodge–Tate weights are the jumps of its ordinary filtration.
hypotheses: Uses the p-adic monodromy theorem (R06.3); for finite residue field (c) was known (Perrin-Riou) by Galois-cohomological dimension counts, which Berger's argument avoids.
Weights ≥ 1 in (b) is the convention HT(χ_p) = +1 (Berger's 'poids ⩾ 1'), e.g. V = Q_p(1).
proofSteps: (a) Lemma 6.4: E is de Rham, hence potentially semistable (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/p-adic-monodromy-theorem); for L/K with E|_{G_L} semistable, 0 → D_st,L(V) → D_st,L(E) → D_st,L(W) → 0 is exact (R06.2), and taking Gal(L/K)-invariants, H^1(Gal(L/K), D_st,L(V)) = 0 (a Q_p-vector space, |Gal(L/K)| invertible) gives dim D_st(E) = dim V + dim W.

(b) Lemma 6.5: weights ≥ 1 give H^1(K, B_dR^+ ⊗ V) = 0 (Hodge–Tate decomposition of V ⊗ C(i), Tate's H^1(K, C(j)) = 0 for j ≠ 0 (R06.2/hodge-tate-decomposition-tate), and 0 → t^{i+1}B_dR^+ → t^iB_dR^+ → C(i) → 0); so 1 ∈ (B_dR^+)^{G_K} lifts to (B_dR^+ ⊗ E)^{G_K} outside (B_dR^+ ⊗ V)^{G_K}, and dim D_dR(E) = dim V + 1.

(c) Corollary 6.3: induction on the length of the ordinary filtration: E = V extension of gr^{i_min} (lowest weight, unramified twist of χ^{i_min}) by Fil^{i_min+1}V (weights > i_min); twisting by the inverse of the character on gr^{i_min} reduces to an extension of Q_p by a de Rham representation of weights ≥ 1, de Rham by (b); then (a) and induction give semistability.
Weights: gr^iV is χ^i times unramified, of Hodge–Tate weight i (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention).
acceptance: V_p(E_q) (Tate curve): ordinary, semistable, not crystalline.
Kummer extensions 0 → Q_p(1) → V → Q_p → 0 (Berger survey II.4.4): all semistable, crystalline iff the Kummer class lies in Q_p ⊗ Ô_K^×.

nodes.title: Ordinarity criteria for two-dimensional crystalline and semistable representations of G_{Q_p}
nodes.statement: Let K = Q_p and V a two-dimensional p-adic representation of G_{Q_p} with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r}, r ≥ 1 (HT(χ_p) = +1). (a) If V is crystalline and not a direct sum of two characters, let f(X) = X² + aX + b ∈ Z_p[X] (v_p(b) = r) be the characteristic polynomial of r(Frob_p) on WD(V), equivalently of φ on D*_cris(V). Then V is reducible — equivalently ordinary, V ≅ (ψ'χ^r *; 0 ψ) with ψ, ψ' unramified — iff f has a root μ ∈ Z_p^×; then ψ(Frob_p) = μ and ψ'(Frob_p) = b/(p^rμ). If f has no unit root (e.g. f irreducible, or a double root), V is irreducible. (b) If V is semistable and not crystalline then r = 2m + 1 is odd, and V is reducible iff m = 0, i.e. r = 1; in that case V is ordinary, a non-split extension of an unramified character ψ by ψχ, with trivial inertial type and N ≠ 0 on WD(V). (c) In particular a two-dimensional semistable non-crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1} (modular weight 2 with inertial Weil–Deligne parameter (id, N ≠ 0)) is ordinary.
hypotheses: K=Q_p and V is two-dimensional over Q_p. The claim that a noncrystalline semistable weight difference is odd is asserted only with Q_p coefficients; it fails for ramified E-coefficients with fractional valuation slopes.
No non-split crystalline extension of ψ'χ^r by ψ exists for r ≥ 1: the weight can only drop up a Jordan–Hölder filtration (Brinon–Conrad after Theorem 8.3.6).
proofSteps: By Colmez–Fontaine (R06.2/colmez-fontaine-theorem), V corresponds to a weakly admissible filtered (φ,N)-module over Q_p with jumps {0, r} (contravariant D*).

(a): Brinon–Conrad Theorem 8.3.6: the only non-trivial weakly admissible subobject is the φ-eigenline for a unit eigenvalue, when it exists; r(Frob_p) on WD(V) has the same characteristic polynomial as φ on D*_cris(V) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/convention-comparison-with-r01 (4)).

(b): Brinon–Conrad Proposition 8.3.8: N ≠ 0 forces eigenvalues λ, pλ; ker N is the φ-stable line of the smaller slope m, and weak admissibility t_H(ker N) = 0 ≤ t_N = m, with equality exactly when m = 0.
Ordinarity: in the reducible cases the sub-object has weight r and the quotient weight 0, which is Berger's ordinary filtration (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-representation).
acceptance: V_p(E) for E/Q_p with good reduction: f = X² − a_pX + p; ordinary iff p ∤ a_p (PARI/GP: y² = x³ − x, p = 5, 13 ordinary; p = 3, 7 supersingular).
V_p(E_q) (Tate curve, r = 1, m = 0): reducible, ordinary, N ≠ 0.
Weight p + 1 (r = p): V ordinary iff f has a unit root; this is the ordinary branch of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/weight-p-plus-one-branch.

nodes.title: Crystalline criterion in weight 2 for every p (including p = 2): Hodge–Tate weights {0,1} ⇔ p-divisible group
nodes.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite (any ramification) and p any prime, including p = 2. (a) A p-adic representation V of G_K is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1} (HT(χ_p) = +1) iff V ≅ V_p(G) = Q_p ⊗ T_p(G) for a p-divisible group G over O_K. (b) V is potentially Barsotti–Tate (V|_{G_L} ≅ V_p(G) for some finite L/K and G over O_L) iff V is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1} and N = 0 on WD(V) (potentially crystalline). (c) For e = 1 and p ≥ 3, (a) and its lattice version are also given by Fontaine–Laffaille ([0, 1] ⊂ [0, p − 2]); for p = 2, or for e > 1, the Fontaine–Laffaille range does not reach weight 1 and (a) rests on the Breuil–Kisin classification (Breuil and Kisin for p > 2; Kisin for connected groups and Kim, Lau, Liu for all groups at p = 2).
hypotheses: The integral classification (G ↦ T_p(G) is an equivalence onto G_K-stable lattices in crystalline representations with weights in {0,1}) is FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4's; this node states the rational criterion in the HT(χ_p) = +1 convention and its potentially crystalline form.
Weights {0,1} in our convention: V_p(G) has det with weight dim G.
proofSteps: (a) ⇐: V_p(G) is crystalline with weights in {0,1} (Fontaine; imported with the R07.4 request). ⇒: R07.4 (Breuil–Kisin: Kisin modules of height ≤ 1, including p = 2).

(b): by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/weil-deligne-descent (b), N = 0 iff V|_{G_L} is crystalline for some L; apply (a) over L; conversely V_p(G) over L is crystalline over L, so V is de Rham with N = 0.
(c): PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-rational-consequences with [0,1] ⊂ [0, p−2] for p ≥ 3 and FL §9 (finite flat groups ↔ MF_tor^{f,2}, R07.3); at p = 2, [0, p−2] = {0}.
acceptance: V_p(E) for E/K with good reduction: crystalline with weights {0, 1}, G = E[p^∞].
V_p(E_q) (Tate curve): weights {0,1} but N ≠ 0, so not potentially Barsotti–Tate.

nodes.title: The endpoint branch: Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p−1] (modular weight p)
nodes.statement: Let K = K_0 = W(k)[1/p] be absolutely unramified (e = 1), σ its Frobenius. A filtered φ-module D over K is weakly admissible in the sense of R06.2/weak-admissibility; its jumps are the i with gr^i D ≠ 0. For Fontaine–Laffaille (FL) objects we use the notation of FL 1982: MF_tor^{f,p} (finite-length W(k)-modules M with M^0 = M, M^p = 0 and φ^i: M^i → M), strongly divisible lattices (FL 7.7), the ring Ŝ and Ŝ_K = K ⊗ Ŝ, and the contravariant functors U_S(M) = Hom_{MF}(M, Ŝ) (lattices), U_S(M) = Ext^1(M, S) (torsion) and U_{S_K}(Δ) = Hom_{MF_K}(Δ, Ŝ_K) (rational), all supplied by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. Let p ≥ 3 and V a crystalline representation of G_K (K = K_0) with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p − 1] (e.g. modular weight k = p: weights {0, p − 1}). (a) Rationally V is covered by Fontaine–Laffaille: V = U_{S_K}(D) = V_cris(D)^* for D = D*_cris(V) with jumps in [0, p−1] (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/small-weight-admissibility, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison), and U_{S_K} is fully faithful there. (b) On strongly divisible lattices with jumps in [0, p − 1], U_S is exact, faithful and rank-preserving, and fully faithful exactly on those M with M/pM in MF_tor^{f,p'} (no nonzero quotient N = N^{p−1}) or in MF_tor^{f,p''} (no nonzero subobject N with N^1 = 0); unrestricted full faithfulness fails (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-endpoint-non-example). (c) The integral statements needed beyond (b) — lattices whose reduction has both a trivial-weight and a weight-(p−1) constituent, and the reductions used in Khare–Wintenberger I Theorem 4.1 at k = p — are supplied by the Breuil–Kisin classification of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4, not by Fontaine–Laffaille.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3 (for p = 2, p − 1 = 1 and the weight-2 case is PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/barsotti-tate-crystalline-criterion).
The §0.9/§6 restrictions are imposed as hypotheses, never replaced by a change of notation.
proofSteps: (a): nodes cited in the statement; the interval [0, p−1] has length p − 1 < p.
(b): FL Proposition 7.15 (R07.3) and the endpoint non-example.
(c): request to R07.4; the ordinary sub-case is decided by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion.
acceptance: Two-dimensional V with weights {0, p−1} over Q_p: V = V_cris(D)^* for D with jumps {0, p−1}, and V is ordinary iff the Frobenius polynomial has a unit root.
Z_p and Z_p(p−1) have isomorphic reductions, so an extension of Z_p(p−1)/p by F_p may have several non-isomorphic FL models — the restricted categories exclude this.

nodes.title: The branch beyond Fontaine–Laffaille: Hodge–Tate weights {0, p} (modular weight p + 1)
nodes.statement: For p≥3, a crystalline E-representation over Q_p with labeled weights {0,p} lies outside the Fontaine–Laffaille interval [0,p−2]. For a weakly admissible two-dimensional contravariant filtered φ-module with jumps {0,p}, a unit φ-eigenvalue gives an ordinary representation; the converse holds by the labeled slope criterion. The crystalline integral lattice and residual calculations beyond the Fontaine–Laffaille interval are supplied by R07.4. Separately, if its residual representation is ordinary in the sense of Khare–Wintenberger Definition 3.4, their Lemma 3.5(i) gives ordinarity at weight p+1 over Q_p. Their weight-two semistable noncrystalline lifting branch is ordinary by Lemma 3.5(ii). These are distinct criteria and distinct weight hypotheses.
hypotheses: p≥3; crystalline weights {0,p} use E-coefficients containing the needed embeddings. Residual-ordinary implications retain exactly the KW base-field and weight hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply weak admissibility to the unit eigenline; use the ordinary labeled slope criterion for the converse. Import integral classification from R07.4 rather than claiming an integral Fontaine–Laffaille realization. Apply the separate KW branches with their explicit hypotheses.
acceptance: Non-example for Fontaine–Laffaille: D with jumps {0, p} has Fil^p D ≠ 0, so it is not an object of MF^{f,p}_K and U_{S_K} is not defined on it.
Ordinary example: ψ'χ^p ⊕ ψ and its non-split crystalline extensions (unique up to isomorphism for given ψ, ψ', Brinon–Conrad after Theorem 8.3.6).

nodes.title: Crystalline comparison for smooth proper O_K-schemes, read through D_cris
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let 𝔛 be a smooth proper O_K-scheme with generic fibre X and special fibre 𝔛_k, and i ≥ 0. Then V^i := H^i_et(X_K̄, Q_p) is a crystalline G_K-representation, and there are natural isomorphisms of filtered φ-modules D_cris(V^i) ≅ H^i_cris(𝔛_k/W(k))[1/p], where the right side carries the crystalline Frobenius and the filtration on K ⊗_{K_0} H^i_cris(𝔛_k/W(k))[1/p] ≅ H^i_dR(X/K) (Berthelot–Ogus) given by the Hodge filtration. Moreover D_dR(V^i) ≅ H^i_dR(X/K) as filtered K-spaces, the isomorphisms are functorial in 𝔛 and compatible with cup products, and gr^a D_dR(V^i) ≅ H^{i−a}(X, Ω^a), so the Hodge–Tate weight −a of V^i has multiplicity h^{a,i−a}: V^i has its weights in [−i, 0].
hypotheses: K/Q_p finite; 𝔛 is a smooth proper O_K-scheme. Apply the proper smooth formal crystalline comparison to its p-adic completion, and the algebraic–analytic étale comparison from H5.
The filtration on the crystalline side is transported along the Berthelot–Ogus de Rham comparison. All invariant, Frobenius and cup-product maps retain these identifications.
proofSteps: Apply the R06.5 formal crystalline comparison to the p-adic completion of 𝔛, and H5 to identify its analytic étale cohomology with algebraic étale cohomology. This gives the G_K- and φ-equivariant B_cris comparison, filtered after extension to B_dR.
Take G_K-invariants using B_cris^{G_K}=K_0. Compare ranks to obtain dim D_cris(V^i)=dim V^i and the crystalline property.
Transport the de Rham filtration along the Berthelot–Ogus map and the proper smooth de Rham comparison. These two specified maps give filtered compatibility.
Functoriality and cup products are inherited from the formal and de Rham comparisons; the P¹-normalized twist map gives the trace convention.
Hodge–de Rham degeneration identifies gr^aD_dR(V^i) with H^{i−a}(X,Ω^a), hence gives Hodge–Tate weights −a.
acceptance: 𝔛 = P^1_{O_K}, i = 2: V^2 = Q_p(−1), D_cris(V^2) = K_0 t with φ = p and single jump 1, matching H^2_cris(P^1_k/W(k)) = W(k) with φ = p; weight −1.
𝔛 an abelian scheme, i = 1: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/abelian-scheme-dcris.
An elliptic curve with good reduction: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/elliptic-curve-ordinary-supersingular.

The rational field comparison is obtained from the proper smooth formal crystalline target.

nodes.title: The filtered φ-module of an abelian scheme: D_cris(V_p(A)) is dual to H^1_cris
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let 𝒜/O_K be an abelian scheme of relative dimension g with generic fibre A and special fibre A_0. (a) V_p(A) is crystalline and D_cris(V_p(A)) ≅ H^1_cris(A_0/W(k))[1/p]^∨ as filtered φ-modules (dual object), because V_p(A) = H^1_et(A_K̄, Q_p)^∨. (b) Its filtration has jumps −1 and 0, each with multiplicity g: dualising the Hodge exact sequence 0 → H^0(A, Ω^1) → H^1_dR(A/K) → H^1(A, O_A) → 0 gives Fil^0 D_dR(V_p(A)) = H^1(A, O_A)^∨ ≅ Lie(A^∨)^∨ and gr^{−1} D_dR(V_p(A)) ≅ H^0(A, Ω^1)^∨ = Lie(A); hence t_H = t_N = −g. (c) (Dieudonné module) H^1_cris(A_0/W(k)) ≅ D(A_0[p^∞])^{(p)} Frobenius-compatibly (Berthelot–Breen–Messing), so the slopes of D_cris(V_p(A)) are the negatives of the Newton slopes of A_0 and lie in [−1, 0]. For g = 1 and W(k) this answers the request of MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.4.
hypotheses: A/O_K is an abelian scheme. Its Tate-module/cohomology duality is supplied by R01.6 and its Hodge exact sequence by A4. The special-fiber p-divisible-group assertion uses the exact crystalline–Dieudonné comparison with the stated variance.
proofSteps: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/crystalline-comparison-good-reduction with i = 1 gives D_cris(H^1_et(A_K̄, Q_p)) ≅ H^1_cris(A_0/W(k))[1/p] with the Hodge filtration.

V_p(A) is the Q_p-dual of H^1_et(A_K̄, Q_p) (R01.6 request; Brinon–Conrad p. 97), and D_cris commutes with duals on crystalline representations (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful).
The dual filtration is Fil^i(D^∨) = (Fil^{1−i} D)^⊥; with Fil^1 H^1_dR = H^0(A, Ω^1) of dimension g (A4 request) this gives the jumps −1 and 0.
t_H = −g is the sum of the jumps; t_N = t_H because D_cris of a crystalline representation is weakly admissible (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissible-implies-weakly-admissible).
(c): Brinon–Conrad Remark 7.3.3 and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2/dieudonne-p-divisible for D(A_0[p^∞]).
acceptance: g = 1: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/elliptic-curve-ordinary-supersingular.
A_0 ordinary: the slopes of D_cris(V_p(A)) are −1 and 0, each with multiplicity g.
A_0 supersingular elliptic: a single slope −1/2 with multiplicity 2.

sources.match: T_p(A) is the Z_p-linear dual of H^1_et, so D_cris(V_p(A)) is the dual of the filtered φ-module of H^1.
Part (c): D(A[p^∞])^{(p)} ≅ H^1_cris(A/W(k)) ≅ H^1_dR(𝒜/W(k)), Hodge filtration matching Fontaine's module of logarithms.

nodes.title: Tate modules of abelian varieties are de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let A/K be an abelian variety of dimension g, with no hypothesis on its reduction. Then V_p(A) is de Rham, D_dR(V_p(A)) ≅ H^1_dR(A/K)^∨ with the dual Hodge filtration, and V_p(A) has Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1, each with multiplicity g. Equivalently (Hodge–Tate decomposition) C_K ⊗_{Q_p} V_p(A) ≅ (C_K(1) ⊗_K Lie(A)) ⊕ (C_K ⊗_K H^1(A, O_A)^∨). When A has good reduction this is Tate's decomposition for the p-divisible group of its Néron model.
hypotheses: Étale cohomology of the algebraic variety is compared with that of its analytification through the H5 request (Huber).
proofSteps: A^an is proper smooth over K; PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/proper-smooth-rational-de-rham-comparison (a) makes H^1_et(A_K̄, Q_p) de Rham with D_dR ≅ H^1_dR(A/K) and its Hodge filtration (H5 request for the comparison with the analytification).
V_p(A) = H^1_et(A_K̄, Q_p)^∨ (R01.6 request) is de Rham with D_dR(V_p(A)) = D_dR(H^1)^∨ (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/ddr-exact-strict-tensor).

dim H^0(A, Ω^1) = dim H^1(A, O_A) = g (A4 request) gives jumps −1 and 0 of multiplicity g; weights are negatives of jumps (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention), and de Rham implies Hodge–Tate with gr D_dR = D_HT (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/de-rham-implies-hodge-tate), which is the decomposition.
Good reduction cross-check: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/hodge-tate-p-divisible for 𝒜[p^∞] gives the same multiplicities (dim 𝒜[p^∞] = g, dim of its Cartier dual = g).
acceptance: det V_p(E) = Q_p(1) has weight 1 = 0 + 1 (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/weil-pairing-duality).
Tate curve: weights {0, 1} (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-filtered-phi-n-module).
Non-example: H^1_et(A_K̄, Q_p) itself has weights 0 and −1; confusing it with V_p(A) flips the sign (see sourceIssue PadicHodgeTheory/E45).

sources.match: Fontaine: V_p(A) is de Rham for every abelian variety A, with D_dR(V_p(A)) dual to H^1_dR(A/K).
Tate's Hodge–Tate decomposition in the good-reduction case.

nodes.title: Weil-pairing duality, Tate twists and the determinant test
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let A/K be an abelian variety with dual A^∨. (a) The Weil pairing T_p(A) × T_p(A^∨) → Z_p(1) is perfect and G_K-equivariant, so V_p(A^∨) ≅ V_p(A)^∨(1) and H^1_et(A_K̄, Q_p) ≅ V_p(A)^∨ ≅ V_p(A^∨)(−1). (b) For B ∈ {B_cris, B_st, B_dR} with V_p(A) B-admissible, D_B(V_p(A^∨)) ≅ D_B(V_p(A))^∨ ⊗ D_B(Q_p(1)) compatibly with φ, N and filtrations, where D_cris(Q_p(1)) = K_0 t^{−1} with φ = p^{−1} and single jump −1. A polarization A → A^∨ gives a G_K-equivariant perfect alternating pairing V_p(A) × V_p(A) → Q_p(1), hence an alternating pairing D_B(V_p(A)) × D_B(V_p(A)) → D_B(Q_p(1)) compatible with φ, N and the filtrations. (c) For an elliptic curve E, det V_p(E) ≅ Q_p(1), so det D_st(V_p(E)) ≅ K_0 t^{−1}: for K_0 = Q_p the linear map φ has determinant p^{−1}, and the two filtration jumps sum to −1. This is the determinant test of the roadmap: with HT(χ) = +1 the determinant has weight +1 and Frobenius p^{−1} on D_cris.
hypotheses: The Weil pairing and polarization pairings are AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 (request); the Tate-module determinant is ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 (request).
proofSteps: (a): the pairings A[p^n] × A^∨[p^n] → μ_{p^n} are perfect and compatible in n (A3 request); pass to the limit. H^1_et(A_K̄, Q_p) = V_p(A)^∨ (R01.6 request), and V_p(A)^∨ ≅ V_p(A^∨)(−1) by (a).

(b): D_B is an exact tensor functor commuting with duals on B-admissible representations (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/ddr-exact-strict-tensor), and D_cris(Q_p(1)) is computed in PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/dcris-of-tate-twists-and-unramified (1).
(c): a perfect alternating pairing on a rank-two V with values in Q_p(1) identifies Λ²V with Q_p(1); D_B commutes with Λ².
acceptance: Tate curve D_q (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-filtered-phi-n-module): det φ = p^{−1}·1 and jumps −1 + 0 = −1.
11a1 at p = 19 (supersingular): the linear φ on D_cris(V_19(E)) has characteristic polynomial X² + 1/19, determinant 1/19.
Sign test: in Brinon–Conrad's covariant weight convention the determinant has weight −1; the dictionary is PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention.

sources.match: Berger states the duality between T_p(A) and H^1_et; as printed the Tate twist is misplaced (sourceIssue PadicHodgeTheory/E45), corrected in (a).

nodes.title: Good ordinary and good supersingular elliptic curves: same Hodge filtration, different Frobenius
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let E/K be an elliptic curve with good reduction E_0 over k = F_q, q = p^f, and a := q + 1 − #E_0(k). Let D = D_cris(V_p(E)), a filtered φ-module of rank 2 over K_0 with jumps −1 and 0. (a) The K_0-linear map φ^f on D has characteristic polynomial X² − (a/q)X + 1/q. (b) E_0 is ordinary (p ∤ a) iff D has slopes −1 and 0; then D = D_{−1} ⊕ D_0 into φ-stable lines, (D_{−1})_K ≠ Fil^0 D_K, and D_{−1} is a weakly admissible subobject, so V_p(E) has a G_K-stable line that is an unramified twist of Q_p(1) (from the formal group); it is the only G_K-stable line unless Fil^0 D_K = (D_0)_K, in which case V_p(E) is the direct sum of it and an unramified line (as for a canonical lift). (c) E_0 is supersingular (p | a) iff D is isoclinic of slope −1/2; then D has no φ-stable K_0-line and V_p(E) is irreducible. (d) Hence good ordinary and good supersingular curves have the same Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1} and the same Hodge polygon, but non-isomorphic φ-modules.
hypotheses: The comparison with Dieudonné modules (Brinon–Conrad Example 8.1.10 via Berthelot–Breen–Messing) is a consistency check; the proof uses Katz–Messing on H^1_cris.
proofSteps: D ≅ H^1_cris(E_0/W(k))[1/p]^∨ (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/abelian-scheme-dcris) ≅ H^1_cris(E_0/W(k))[1/p] ⊗ D_cris(Q_p(1)) by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/weil-pairing-duality (a) with E = E^∨.

Katz–Messing (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective): φ^f on H^1_cris(E_0/W(k)) ⊗ K_0 has characteristic polynomial X² − aX + q; tensoring with D_cris(Q_p(1)), where φ^f = q^{−1}, gives (a).

Newton polygon of X² − aX + q: root valuations {0, f} if p ∤ a and {f/2, f/2} if p | a (|a| ≤ 2√q); divide by f and shift by −1. The slope decomposition (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/slope-decomposition) gives D = D_{−1} ⊕ D_0 in the ordinary case; a φ-stable line has integral slope (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/newton-number-tN), so none exists in the supersingular case.

Subrepresentations of a crystalline V correspond to weakly admissible φ-stable subobjects with the induced filtration (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/crystalline-subobjects-strict). For D_{−1}: t_N = −1, and t_H(D_{−1}) = −1 unless (D_{−1})_K = Fil^0, which weak admissibility of D excludes (t_H would be 0 > t_N). D_0 is a subobject with t_H = t_N only if Fil^0 = (D_0)_K (the split case); otherwise it is not a subrepresentation.
Consistency with Dieudonné theory: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2/elliptic-dieudonne (ordinary ⇔ M1, supersingular ⇔ M2).
acceptance: 11a1, p = 3: a_3 = −1 (ordinary); X² + X/3 + 1/3 has root valuations −1 and 0 (point count by script).
11a1, p = 19: a_19 = 0 (supersingular); X² + 1/19 has both roots of valuation −1/2.
11a1, p = 2: a_2 = −2 (supersingular); X² + X + 1/2 has both roots of valuation −1/2.
All three have jumps −1 and 0: the required example "same Hodge weights, different Frobenius structures".

sources.match: The ordinary case: φ(x) = α_0p^{−1}x, φ(y) = β_0y with α_0, β_0 ∈ O_F^×, and Fil^0 = F(y + λx).
The supersingular case: no φ-stable line.
Same Hodge polygon, Newton polygon depending on ordinary versus supersingular.

nodes.title: The Kummer representation V(q) of an element q ∈ K^×
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Fix a compatible system ε = (ε^{(n)})_n of primitive p^n-th roots of unity. For q ∈ K^× choose q̃ = (q^{(n)})_n with q^{(0)} = q and (q^{(n+1)})^p = q^{(n)}, and define c_q: G_K → Z_p by g(q^{(n)}) = q^{(n)}(ε^{(n)})^{c_q(g)} for all n. Then c_q is a continuous 1-cocycle, c_q(gh) = c_q(g) + χ(g)c_q(h), and T(q) = Z_p e ⊕ Z_p f with g e = χ(g)e, g f = f + c_q(g)e is a continuous Z_p[G_K]-module; V(q) := Q_p ⊗ T(q). (i) 0 → Z_p(1) → T(q) → Z_p → 0 is exact and its class in H^1(K, Z_p(1)) is the Kummer class δ(q). (ii) Another choice of q̃ changes c_q by a coboundary, so V(q) is well defined up to isomorphism of extensions. (iii) V(q) ≅ V(q^a) as representations for every integer a ≠ 0. (iv) V(q) is split iff q is a root of unity. (v) The classes δ(q), q ∈ K^×, span H^1(K, Q_p(1)) ≅ Q_p ⊗ K̂^× (K̂^× the p-adic completion) over Q_p, and q ↦ (v_p(q), log_K(q)) induces an isomorphism Q_p ⊗ K̂^× ≅ Q_p ⊕ K.
hypotheses: Continuous cohomology with Z_p(1) and Q_p(1) coefficients and the Kummer isomorphism are supplied by ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1; the construction itself uses only the explicit cocycle.
proofSteps: c_q(g) mod p^n is well defined: g(q^{(n)})/q^{(n)} is a p^n-th root of unity, and the compatibility of q̃ and ε under p-th powers makes the residues compatible, so c_q(g) ∈ Z_p = lim Z/p^n.
Cocycle: gh(q^{(n)}) = g(q^{(n)}(ε^{(n)})^{c_q(h)}) = q^{(n)}(ε^{(n)})^{c_q(g) + χ(g)c_q(h)}. Continuity: c_q mod p^n factors through Gal(K(ε^{(n)}, q^{(n)})/K).
(ii): replacing q̃ by q̃·ε^b (b ∈ Z_p) changes c_q by g ↦ (χ(g) − 1)b; f ↦ f + be identifies the two modules.
(iii): with the system (q^{(n)})^a one has c_{q^a} = a c_q, and e ↦ ae, f ↦ f is a G_K-isomorphism V(q) → V(q^a).

(i), (iv), (v): Kummer theory (R02.1 request): the connecting map of 0 → μ_{p^n} → K̄^× → K̄^× → 0 sends q to the class of g ↦ g(q^{(n)})/q^{(n)}, i.e. c_q mod p^n; on Q_p ⊗ K^× its kernel is the image of the roots of unity; K^× = π_K^Z × μ(K) × (1 + m_K) with 1 + m_K a Z_p-module, so every element of Q_p ⊗ K̂^× is p^{−n}(a ⊗ π_K) + p^{−n} ⊗ u with u ∈ 1 + m_K, and log: Q_p ⊗ (1 + m_K) ≅ K (Brinon–Conrad Lemma 8.3.9, proof).
acceptance: q = p, K = Q_p: T(p) is the Tate module of the Tate curve E_p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-tate-module).
q a root of unity: c_q is a coboundary and V(q) ≅ Q_p(1) ⊕ Q_p.
q = 1 + p, K = Q_p, p odd: V(q) is the non-split crystalline extension of Brinon–Conrad Example 9.2.8.

sources.match: The matrix (χ η_u; 0 1) realises the Kummer class of u.
H^1(K, Q_p(1)) = Q_p ⊗ K̂^×, an extension of Q_p by Q_p ⊗ (1 + m_K) ≅ K.
All extensions of Q_p by Q_p(1) come from Kummer theory.

uses.how: D_st(V(q)) is computed from the periods t and λ_st(q̃).
T_p(E_q) ≅ T(q) through Tate's uniformisation.
the L-invariant classifies the non-crystalline V(q) up to isomorphism.
acceptance item "Kummer extensions 0 → Q_p(1) → V → Q_p → 0".
every extension of Q_p by Q_p(1) is a Kummer extension.

nodes.title: Extensions of Q_p by Q_p(1) are semistable, with an explicit filtered (φ,N)-module
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let q ∈ K^× and V = V(q) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/kummer-representation). (a) V is semistable: with u_q := λ_st(q̃) ∈ B_st^+ (so g(u_q) = u_q + c_q(g)t, φ(u_q) = pu_q, N(u_q) = −v_p(q)), the elements x = t^{−1} ⊗ e and y = −u_q t^{−1} ⊗ e + 1 ⊗ f form a K_0-basis of D_st(V) with φ(x) = p^{−1}x, φ(y) = y, N(x) = 0, N(y) = v_p(q)x. (b) In D_dR(V) = K ⊗_{K_0} D_st(V) (embedding with log_K(p) = 0): Fil^{−1} = D_dR(V), Fil^0 = K(y + log_K(q)x), Fil^1 = 0; so V has Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1 and t_H = t_N = −1. (c) V is crystalline iff v_p(q) = 0, and then D_cris(V) = D_st(V). (d) Every extension of Q_p by Q_p(1) is semistable, and the crystalline classes form the Q_p-hyperplane Q_p ⊗ Ô_K^× (≅ K via log) of H^1(K, Q_p(1)) ≅ Q_p ⊗ K̂^×, which has dimension [K : Q_p] + 1.
hypotheses: For K = Q_p this is Berger's computation (survey II.4.3–II.4.4); for ramified K the same formulas hold with v_p(q) ∈ (1/e)Z and λ_st of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring in place of Berger's log[q̃] = v_p(q)Y + log[q̃/p̃^{v_p(q)}].
Brinon–Conrad's monodromy operator is −N; with their N the sign of N(y) changes.
proofSteps: Invariance: g(x) = χ(g)^{−1}t^{−1} ⊗ χ(g)e = x and g(y) = −(u_q + c_q(g)t)χ(g)^{−1}t^{−1} ⊗ χ(g)e + 1 ⊗ (f + c_q(g)e) = y (Berger II.4.3).

x and y are B_st-linearly independent (triangular coordinates), so dim_{K_0} D_st(V) ≥ 2 = dim V; B_st is regular (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-rings-are-regular), so V is semistable and x, y is a basis (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissibility-dimension-bound).
φ(t) = pt and φ(u_q) = pu_q give φ(x) = p^{−1}x and φ(y) = y; N(t) = 0 and N(u_q) = −v_p(q) give N(y) = v_p(q)x.

Filtration: ι(u_q) = log_dR([q̃]/q) + log_K(q) with [q̃]/q ≡ 1 mod ker θ (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bst-embedding-into-bdr), so ι(u_q) − log_K(q) ∈ tB_dR^+ and y + log_K(q)x = −(ι(u_q) − log_K(q))t^{−1} ⊗ e + 1 ⊗ f ∈ B_dR^+ ⊗ V. x ∉ Fil^0 since t^{−1} ∉ B_dR^+, and y + log_K(q)x ∉ Fil^1 since its f-coordinate is 1 ∉ tB_dR^+.

(c): D_cris(V) = D_st(V)^{N=0} (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/crystalline-semistable-de-rham-implications) is K_0x when v_p(q) ≠ 0; when q ∈ O_K^×, u_q = λ(q̃) lies in B_cris^+ (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-logarithm).

(d): semistable representations are closed under direct sums and subquotients (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissible-category-tannakian); a Baer sum of extensions is a subquotient of their direct sum, and the δ(q) span H^1(K, Q_p(1)) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/kummer-representation (v)). The crystalline classes are those of units by (c) (Brinon–Conrad Lemma 8.3.9).

q = 1 + p, K = Q_p, p odd: crystalline, Fil^0 = Q_p(y + log_p(1 + p)x) with v_p(log_p(1 + p)) = 1.
Non-example: a non-split extension of Q_p(1) by Q_p (the opposite order) is not de Rham (Brinon–Conrad Example 6.3.5, recorded under PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2), so (d) does not extend to it.

nodes.title: The Tate module of the Tate curve is the Kummer lattice of q
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let q ∈ K^× with 0 < |q| < 1 and E_q the Tate curve over K (y² + xy = x³ + a_4(q)x + a_6(q), split multiplicative reduction, j(E_q) = 1/q + 744 + 196884q + ⋯). Tate's G_K-equivariant uniformisation α: K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄) restricts to isomorphisms {x ∈ K̄^×/q^Z : x^{p^n} ∈ q^Z} ≅ E_q[p^n](K̄), whose source consists of the p^{2n} classes (ε^{(n)})^i(q^{(n)})^j, 0 ≤ i, j ≤ p^n − 1. In the limit, T_p(E_q) ≅ T(q) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/kummer-representation), G_K-equivariantly, with lim α(ε^{(n)}) ↦ e and lim α(q^{(n)}) ↦ f; so 0 → Z_p(1) → T_p(E_q) → Z_p → 0 is exact with class δ(q), the sub Z_p(1) being the image of μ_{p^∞}.
hypotheses: Tate's uniformisation and its Galois equivariance are the Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 target (request); the Tate module as a G_K-module is ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 (request).
proofSteps: If x^{p^n} = q^m then x = (q^{(n)})^m ζ with ζ^{p^n} = 1, and modulo q^Z only m mod p^n matters; so the p^n-torsion of K̄^×/q^Z is free over Z/p^n on the classes of ε^{(n)} and q^{(n)}, with p^{2n} elements (Berger II.4.2, index range corrected: sourceIssue PadicHodgeTheory/E42).
α is G_K-equivariant, so g acts on α(ε^{(n)}) through χ(g) and on α(q^{(n)}) by q^{(n)} ↦ q^{(n)}(ε^{(n)})^{c_q(g)}.
α is a homomorphism, so p·α(q^{(n+1)}) = α(q^{(n)}) and p·α(ε^{(n+1)}) = α(ε^{(n)}); the two systems give a Z_p-basis of T_p(E_q) with the Galois action of T(q).
acceptance: 11a1 at p = 11 (split multiplicative, a_11 = 1): the q ∈ Q_11 with j(E_q) = −122023936/161051 has v_11(q) = 5 = v_11(Δ) (inverting j = 1/q + 744 + 196884q + ⋯ in a script; j(q) agrees with j(E) to 11^60).
p-torsion: E_q[p](K̄) ≅ (Z/p)² generated by α(ζ_p) and α(q^{1/p}).

sources.match: ε^{(n)} and q^{(n)} give a basis of E_q[p^n] and of T_p(E_q), with g(f) = f + c(g)e.

nodes.title: The filtered (φ,N)-module of the Tate curve
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). With q and E_q as in PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-tate-module, V = V_p(E_q) is semistable and not crystalline, and D_st(V) ≅ D_q := K_0x ⊕ K_0y with φ(x) = p^{−1}x, φ(y) = y, N(x) = 0, N(y) = v_p(q)x, and on D_{q,K}: Fil^{−1} = D_{q,K}, Fil^0 = K(y + log_K(q)x), Fil^1 = 0. Consequently V has Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}; D_q is weakly admissible with t_H = t_N = −1, its only nonzero proper subobject being K_0x = ker N; V is not potentially crystalline (N ≠ 0 on WD(V)), hence not potentially Barsotti–Tate although its weights are {0, 1}; V is ordinary with ordinary filtration Q_p(1) ⊂ V. For K = Q_p, D_q is the module that PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/tate-curve-weil-deligne-example takes as given; this node discharges that hypothesis. V is the stage's example of a de Rham representation that is not crystalline.
hypotheses: q ∈ K^× with 0 < |q| < 1, so v_p(q) > 0; log_K(p) = 0 fixes the filtration (another choice of log_K(p) ∈ K_0 moves the line by a K_0-multiple of x).
proofSteps: T_p(E_q) ≅ T(q) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-tate-module); apply PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/kummer-representations-semistable (a)–(c) with v_p(q) > 0.

Weak admissibility: t_H(D_q) = −1 + 0 = −1 and t_N(D_q) = −1 + 0 = −1. A (φ, N)-stable line lies in ker N = K_0x (a φ-stable line through y + cx is not N-stable); t_H(K_0x) = −1 because Fil^0 is not K·x, and t_N(K_0x) = −1 (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/weak-admissibility).

Not potentially crystalline: N ≠ 0 on WD(V) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/weil-deligne-descent (b)); hence not potentially Barsotti–Tate (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/barsotti-tate-crystalline-criterion (b)).
Ordinary: the filtration Q_p(1) = V(1)-part ⊂ V with quotient Q_p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-representation).
acceptance: 11a1 at p = 11: φ = diag(1/11, 1), N = (0 5; 0 0), Fil^0 = Q_11(y + log_11(q)x) with log_11(q) = 5L, L ≡ 11·10225 mod 11^5 (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-l-invariant).
Weil–Deligne check (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/tate-curve-weil-deligne-example): r(Φ) = φ^{−1} = diag(11, 1) with characteristic polynomial (X − 11)(X − a_11), a_11 = 1.
Non-example for "de Rham ⇒ crystalline": V_p(E_q) is de Rham, even semistable, but not crystalline.

nodes.title: The L-invariant of a semistable non-crystalline extension of Q_p by Q_p(1)
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Call D ∈ MF^{φ,N,wa}_K of Tate type if dim_{K_0} D = 2, N ≠ 0, the filtration jumps are −1 and 0, and D^{φ=1} contains an element y with N(y) ≠ 0; by Colmez–Fontaine and PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/kummer-representations-semistable these are the D_st(V) of the non-crystalline extensions V of Q_p by Q_p(1). The L-invariant L(D) ∈ K is the unique element with y + L(D)·N(y) ∈ Fil^0 D_K for y ∈ D^{φ=1} ∖ {0}. It does not depend on y (D^{φ=1} is a Q_p-line and y ↦ ay scales N(y) by a), and it exists because Fil^0 D_K ≠ K·N(y) by weak admissibility. For V = V(q) with v_p(q) ≠ 0: L(V) := L(D_st(V)) = log_K(q)/v_p(q); in particular the Tate curve has L(E_q) = log_K(q)/v_p(q), which for K = Q_p is log_p(q)/ord_p(q). Classification: for v_p(q), v_p(q′) ≠ 0, V(q) ≅ V(q′) iff L(q) = L(q′); E_q and its isogenous curve E_{q^n} have the same L.
hypotheses: Fix the embedding K→C and the branch log_p(p)=0. The denominator is ord_p(q)>0; the ratio, rather than the unnormalized logarithm, is the isomorphism invariant in this convention.
proofSteps: In D_st(V(q)) take y as in PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/kummer-representations-semistable: φ(y) = y, N(y) = v_p(q)x and Fil^0 = K(y + log_K(q)x) = K(y + (log_K(q)/v_p(q))N(y)).
Independence of y: D^{φ=1} = Q_p y (φ is σ-semilinear, (K_0)^{σ=1} = Q_p), and replacing y by ay replaces N(y) by aN(y).
Existence: if Fil^0 D_K = K·N(y) then the subobject K_0N(y) = ker N has t_H = 0 > −1 = t_N, contradicting weak admissibility (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/weak-admissibility; Brinon–Conrad p. 124).

Classification: V(q) ≅ V(q′) iff δ(q′) ∈ Q_p^× δ(q) (a non-split extension of Q_p by Q_p(1) determines its class up to Q_p^×) iff (v_p(q′), log_K(q′)) is proportional to (v_p(q), log_K(q)) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/kummer-representation (v)) iff L(q) = L(q′). Equivalently D_st is fully faithful (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful) and Tate-type modules are isomorphic iff their L agree (scale x, y).
E_q → E_{q^n}, induced by x ↦ x^n on K̄^×, is an isogeny, and L(q^n) = n log_K(q)/(n v_p(q)) = L(q).
acceptance: 11a1 at p = 11: v_11(q) = 5, v_11(L) = 1 and L ≡ 11·10225 mod 11^5 (computed from the q-expansion of j and log_11(u) = log_11(u^{10})/10 for the unit part u).
q = p: L = 0 (log_p(p) = 0).

nodes.title: The p-adic criterion of good reduction: good reduction iff V_p(A) is crystalline
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let A/K be an abelian variety of dimension g. (a) A has good reduction (it extends to an abelian scheme 𝒜 over O_K) iff V_p(A) is crystalline; then T_p(A) = T_p(𝒜[p^∞]), V_p(A) has Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1 with multiplicity g, and D_cris(V_p(A)) is PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/abelian-scheme-dcris. (b) A has potentially good reduction iff V_p(A) is potentially crystalline iff N = 0 on WD(V_p(A)). (c) For an elliptic curve E/K with minimal Weierstrass equation W over O_K: W.HasGoodReduction (Mathlib) iff V_p(E) is crystalline, and E has potentially good reduction (v(j(E)) ≥ 0) iff N = 0 on WD(V_p(E)). V_p(A) is never unramified for g ≥ 1 (weight 1 occurs), so unramifiedness, the ℓ ≠ p criterion of Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5), is not the criterion at p.
hypotheses: A/K is an abelian variety. Use the good-reduction criterion that A[p^infinity] extends over O_K, supplied by R11.3, and the integral crystalline lattice classifier from R07.4 at its actual base-field hypotheses.
proofSteps: (a) ⇒: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.6/abelian-scheme-torsion-finite-flat gives 𝒜[p^∞] over O_K of height 2g with T_p(A) = T_p(𝒜[p^∞]); for every p-divisible group G over O_K, T_p(G)[1/p] is crystalline with weights in {0, 1} (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/crystalline-01-is-bt); the multiplicities are dim 𝒜[p^∞] = g and the dimension of its Cartier dual 𝒜^∨[p^∞], also g (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/hodge-tate-p-divisible).

(a) ⇐: V_p(A) has weights in {0, 1} (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/abelian-variety-hodge-tate-weights); if it is crystalline, the lattice form of R07.4/crystalline-01-is-bt gives a p-divisible group G over O_K with T_p(G) ≅ T_p(A). Finite étale K-group schemes are Galois modules, so G_K ≅ A[p^∞]: A[p^∞] extends to O_K, and Grothendieck's criterion (R11.3 request) gives good reduction.

(b): potentially good reduction means good reduction over some finite L/K; by (a) over L this is crystallinity of V_p(A)|_{G_L}, and for de Rham V (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/abelian-variety-hodge-tate-weights) potentially crystalline ⇔ N = 0 on WD(V) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/weil-deligne-descent (b)).

(c): HasGoodReduction of a minimal equation says the minimal model is an elliptic curve over O_K (Mathlib hasGoodReduction_iff_isElliptic_reduction), i.e. an abelian scheme of relative dimension 1 (NeronModels R11.1 request); potentially good reduction ⇔ v(j) ≥ 0 is the EllipticCurves Layer 4 statement (request).
acceptance: 11a1 at p = 3: good ordinary reduction, V_3(E) crystalline (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/elliptic-curve-ordinary-supersingular).
11a1 at p = 11: split multiplicative, V_11(E) semistable, not crystalline (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-filtered-phi-n-module).
Non-example: V_p(E) is ramified even for good reduction (its Hodge–Tate weight 1), unlike V_ℓ(E), ℓ ≠ p.

nodes.title: Abelian varieties with semistable reduction have semistable Tate modules
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let A/K be an abelian variety with semistable reduction (the identity component of the special fibre of its Néron model is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus). Then V_p(A) is semistable, and N = 0 on D_st(V_p(A)) iff A has good reduction. Explicitly, Raynaud's uniformisation A^an = G^an/Γ, with 0 → T → G → B → 0 (T a torus of rank r split by an unramified extension, B an abelian variety with good reduction, Γ ≅ Z^r a lattice with unramified G_K-action), gives a G_K-stable filtration 0 ⊆ V_t ⊆ V_f ⊆ V_p(A) with V_t ≅ V_p(T) (an unramified twist of Q_p(1)^r), V_f/V_t ≅ V_p(B) and V_p(A)/V_f ≅ Γ ⊗ Q_p (unramified), all graded pieces crystalline. Since every abelian variety acquires semistable reduction over a finite extension, V_p(A) is potentially semistable in general.
hypotheses: Raynaud's uniformisation and Grothendieck's semistable reduction theorem are supplied by NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3.
That N has rank r (Grothendieck's monodromy pairing; Coleman–Iovita identify Fontaine's N with it) belongs to NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.4–R11.5 and is not claimed here.
proofSteps: V_p(A) is de Rham (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/abelian-variety-hodge-tate-weights).

The graded pieces are crystalline: unramified twists of Q_p(1)^r and unramified representations by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/dcris-of-tate-twists-and-unramified; V_p(B) by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/good-reduction-iff-crystalline (a).

V_f is de Rham, as a subrepresentation of a de Rham representation (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissible-category-tannakian), and an extension of V_p(B) by V_t, so it is semistable by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-implies-semistable (a); V_p(A) is a de Rham extension of V_p(A)/V_f by V_f, hence semistable by the same theorem.

N = 0 iff V_p(A) is crystalline (D_cris = D_st^{N=0}, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/crystalline-semistable-de-rham-implications) iff A has good reduction (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/good-reduction-iff-crystalline (a)).
Potential semistability: semistable reduction over a finite L/K (R11.3 request) and the above over L.
acceptance: Elliptic curves: r = 1 for multiplicative reduction, B = 0, V_t = Q_p(1) up to the unramified quadratic twist (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/multiplicative-reduction-elliptic-curves).

nodes.title: Elliptic curves with potentially multiplicative reduction
nodes.statement: Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K̄ an algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), χ the p-adic cyclotomic character, v_p the valuation with v_p(p) = 1 and log_K the Iwasawa logarithm on K̄^× (log_K(p) = 0, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar). Period functors are covariant, D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K}, N = −d/du on B_st (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring), and Hodge–Tate weights follow HT(χ) = +1 (weights are the negatives of the jumps of D_dR). Let E/K be an elliptic curve with v(j(E)) < 0 and W a minimal Weierstrass equation over O_K; let q ∈ K^× be the unique element with 0 < |q| < 1 and j(E_q) = j(E). (a) If W.HasSplitMultiplicativeReduction (Mathlib), E ≅ E_q over K, V_p(E) ≅ V(q) and D_st(V_p(E)) ≅ D_q (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-filtered-phi-n-module). (b) If W.HasMultiplicativeReduction but not split, E is the twist of E_q by the unramified quadratic character η of G_K, V_p(E) ≅ V(q) ⊗ η is semistable and not crystalline, and D_st(V_p(E)) ≅ D_q ⊗ D_cris(η); for K = Q_p: φ(x) = −p^{−1}x, φ(y) = −y, N(y) = v_p(q)x, same filtration. (c) If W has additive reduction, E is the twist of E_q by a ramified quadratic character ψ, and V_p(E) ≅ V(q) ⊗ ψ is potentially semistable, not semistable, with WD(V_p(E)) ≅ WD(V(q)) ⊗ rec(ψ) (inertia acting through ψ, N ≠ 0). In all three cases V_p(E) is not potentially crystalline.
hypotheses: Use the G_K-equivariant Tate uniformization and quadratic-twist classification from TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 4, with its minimal-model and residue-characteristic hypotheses. For v(j)<0 the twisting character is unramified exactly when the reduction is multiplicative.
proofSteps: Tate's theorem (EllipticCurves Layer 4 request) gives the unique q and the twist; V_p of a quadratic twist by γ is V_p ⊗ γ.
(a): PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-filtered-phi-n-module.

(b): D_st is a tensor functor (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful); D_cris(η) = K_0e with φe = λe, λ = −1 for K = Q_p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/dcris-of-tate-twists-and-unramified (3)); a semistable representation tensored with a crystalline one is semistable; N is unchanged, so V is not crystalline.

(c): ψ is trivial on G_L for the quadratic extension L it cuts out, so V|_{G_L} ≅ V(q)|_{G_L} is semistable (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/crystalline-semistable-base-change); V is not semistable because WD(V)|_{I_K} contains ψ|_{I_K} ≠ 1 (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/weil-deligne-descent (b)).
Twisting by a character does not change N ≠ 0, so no case is potentially crystalline (R06.3/weil-deligne-descent (b)).
acceptance: 11a1 at p = 11: a_11 = 1, split; case (a) with v_11(q) = 5.
15a1 at p = 3: a_3 = −1, non-split (point count by script); case (b): φ = −diag(1/3, 1), N = (0 4; 0 0), v_3(q) = v_3(Δ) = 4 (Δ(15a1) = 15^4).
15a1 at p = 5: a_5 = 1, split; case (a).
Case (c): the twist of 11a1 by the quadratic character of Q_11(√−11) has additive reduction at 11 and v_11(j) < 0.

nodes.title: p-adic local–global compatibility for abelian varieties at places of good reduction
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, A/F an abelian variety of dimension g, v a place of F above p at which A has good reduction A_v over k_v = F_{q_v} (q_v = p^{f_v}), and ℓ ≠ p. Let P_v(X) = det(X − Frob_v | V_ℓ(A)) for an arithmetic Frobenius Frob_v; it lies in Z[X], is independent of ℓ ≠ p and is the characteristic polynomial of the Frobenius endomorphism of A_v. Then V_p(A)|_{G_{F_v}} is crystalline and: (a) the K_0-linear map φ^{f_v} on D_cris(H^1_et(A_{F̄_v}, Q_p)) ≅ H^1_cris(A_v/W(k_v))[1/p] has characteristic polynomial P_v(X); (b) WD(V_p(A)|_{G_{F_v}}) is unramified with N = 0 and arithmetic Frobenius of characteristic polynomial P_v(X), so WD(V_p(A)|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ WD(V_ℓ(A)|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} after any field isomorphism Q̄_p ≅ Q̄_ℓ; (c) for an elliptic curve with multiplicative reduction at v the p-adic and ℓ-adic Weil–Deligne representations agree as well, with N ≠ 0. These are the coefficient-prime inputs consumed by AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.5 and by the local-factor comparisons of NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5.
hypotheses: Nothing here determines the Weil–Deligne parameter at a place above the coefficient prime for a general (almost strictly) compatible system without the extra hypothesis of the source; the node is about Tate modules of abelian varieties.
ℓ-adic inputs (unramifiedness at good places, P_v, smooth proper base change) are supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6.
proofSteps: Crystalline: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/good-reduction-iff-crystalline (a) over F_v.

(a): D_cris(H^1) ≅ H^1_cris(A_v/W(k_v))[1/p] (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/crystalline-comparison-good-reduction); Katz–Messing (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective) gives det(1 − tφ^{f_v} | H^1_cris ⊗ K_0) = det(1 − t·Frob_geom | H^1_et(A_{v,k̄_v}, Q_ℓ)); smooth proper base change identifies the latter with H^1_et(A_{F̄_v}, Q_ℓ) = V_ℓ(A)^∨, on which geometric Frobenius has the eigenvalues of arithmetic Frobenius on V_ℓ(A) (R01.6 request).

(b): for crystalline V, Fontaine's recipe (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/weil-deligne-parameter, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/fontaine-weil-deligne-functor) gives WD(V) = D_cris(V) with N = 0, trivial inertia and arithmetic Frobenius the linearisation of φ^{−f}; on D_cris(V_p(A)) = D_cris(H^1)^∨ (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/plan/abelian-scheme-dcris) its eigenvalues are those of φ^f on D_cris(H^1), the roots of P_v. V_ℓ(A) is unramified at v with the same characteristic polynomial, so the Frobenius-semisimplifications agree.

(c): split case by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/tate-curve-weil-deligne-example with D_st(V_p(E)) ≅ D_q (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/tate-curve-filtered-phi-n-module); non-split by twisting both sides by η (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/plan/multiplicative-reduction-elliptic-curves (b)).
acceptance: 11a1, v = 3: P_3 = X² + X + 3 (a_3 = −1); on D_cris(V_3(E)) the linear φ has characteristic polynomial X² + X/3 + 1/3, and the arithmetic Frobenius of WD has X² + X + 3.
11a1 at 11 (multiplicative): characteristic polynomial (X − 11)(X − 1) on both sides (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/tate-curve-weil-deligne-example).

nodes.title: De Rham completion over an algebraically closed field
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of mixed characteristic (0,p), with rank-one valuation and 0<|p|<1. On the existing carrier BDeRhamPlus(O_C,p), θ extends to a surjective map θ_dR:B_dR^+(C)→C. Its kernel is generated by the image of any generator ξ of ker(θ:A_inf(C)[1/p]→C). The ring is a complete DVR for this ideal, its residue field is C, and BDeRham(O_C,p) is canonically its fraction field. For C=ℂ_p the maps coincide with Mathlib’s fontaineTheta and its localization. The natural topology is the inverse-limit topology of the Banach quotients; it is distinguished from the discrete valuation topology.
hypotheses: C as above; O_C is the valuation ring, with the shared tilt and θ map; p-adic completeness refers to O_C, not to C.
proofSteps: Import principal-kernel and regular-generator properties of θ from AI.0:integral. Apply completion to A_inf[1/p], identify every ξ-adic quotient and its residue map, and prove separation and regularity. Use the associated graded C[ξ] to show that every nonzero element is a unit times a power of ξ. Identify Mathlib’s localization at all generators with localization at ξ, hence with the fraction field.
acceptance: The residue is C rather than O_C; ξ is a nonunit in the completed ring although p is a unit.
The statement applies to C beyond the completed algebraic closure of a finite extension of Q_p; no G_K-action is asserted without an action on C.

sources.locator: Definition 6.1, Lemma 6.3, Corollary 6.4, printed pp.35–36 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: The perfectoid completion and its principal residue ideal specialize at any complete algebraically closed field.
The residue map and discrete valuation structure follow from the principal regular kernel.

nodes.title: Breuil’s completed semistable periods
nodes.statement: For K a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic with perfect residue k and uniformizer π, put W=W(k), K_0=W[1/p]. Let R_l be the PD envelope of W[t]/p^l→O_K/p^l, t↦π, compatible with the canonical divided powers of p. Let P_l be H^0_log-cris((Spec(O_Kbar/p),O_Kbar∖{0})/(Spec R_l,N→R_l,1↦t)). Define S^min_0=lim_l R_l, 𝒦=S^min_0[1/p], Â_st=lim_l P_l and B̂_st^+=Â_st[1/p]. For compatible p-power roots of π, Â_st identifies with the p-adic completion of A_cris⟨X⟩. In these coordinates φ(X)=(1+X)^p−1, N(X)=1+X, g(X)=[ε_π(g)](1+X)−1, and the structural image of t is [π^flat](1+X)^−1. Thus N(t)=−t and φ(t)=t^p. This N convention gives Nφ=pφN; replacing the sign requires replacing it everywhere, including the B_st embedding.
hypotheses: All divided powers are compatible with those on p; P_l uses logarithmic crystalline cohomology from CR.6.
The name t in R_l is a polynomial variable; Fontaine’s period is denoted t_Fontaine when both occur.
proofSteps: Use the universal PD and log-crystalline objects supplied by CR.0 and CR.6. Compute P_l after choosing roots of π as W_l(O_Kbar/p)^DP⟨X⟩ with the transition maps specified by Frobenius on Witt coordinates. Pass to inverse limits, then invert p. Transport the canonical operators and check independence of the chosen roots by the coordinate change X↦[ε]^{-1}(1+X′)−1.
acceptance: Changing roots transports the ring and all operators; it does not change its isomorphism class.

nodes.title: Nilpotent and completed semistable periods
nodes.statement: With these rings, B_st^+ identifies canonically with the elements of B̂_st^+ killed by some power of N. The ring B̂_st^+ is flat over 𝒦, N:B̂_st^+→B̂_st^+ is surjective, and its G_K-invariants are 𝒦. For a finite-dimensional (φ,N)-module D with nilpotent N, the diagonal-monodromy sequences 0→(D⊗B_st^+)^{N=0}→D⊗B_st^+→D⊗B_st^+→0 and 0→(D⊗B̂_st^+)^{N=0}→D⊗B̂_st^+→D⊗B̂_st^+→0 are exact and their left terms agree.
hypotheses: K,π and compatible period embeddings as in the construction; N on D is nilpotent.
proofSteps: Identify the N-nilpotent coordinate subring with polynomials in log(1+X), then compare with the chosen B_st^+ coordinate. Use the flatness theorem for completed log-crystalline periods. Derive surjectivity by solving N at each P_l and proving R^1lim ker N_l=0. Apply exp(−log(1+X)N_D) to reduce the tensor-monodromy statement to scalar periods.
acceptance: For D=K_0 and N=0 the two kernels are B_cris^+.
Flatness and the inverse-limit vanishing are required; pointwise surjectivity alone is insufficient.

nodes.title: Frobenius-isotypic monodromy edge maps
nodes.statement: For every integer r and nilpotent finite-dimensional (φ,N)-module D, the edge map ((D⊗_{K_0}𝒦)/N(D⊗𝒦))^{φ=p^r}→H^1(G_K,(D⊗B_st^+)^{N=0}) coming from the completed-monodromy row factors through specialization t↦0 to D/ND. The map is compared with the edge map of the B_st^+ row through the common N=0 term. No factorization of an unrestricted monodromy cokernel, and no equality of invariant images of N, is asserted.
hypotheses: The period embedding and sign convention of the completed-period comparison are fixed.
proofSteps: Take continuous G_K-cohomology of the two exact rows and compare their connecting maps by naturality. Restrict to φ=p^r. Apply the specialization computation in Lemma B.14; the restriction is essential.
acceptance: The case D=K_0,r=0 includes constants but does not identify ker(𝒦→K_0) with N of invariant completed periods.

nodes.title: Period functors over a perfect residue field
nodes.statement: For K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with perfect residue k of characteristic p, put K_0=Frac W(k) and C=completed Kbar. Extend the existing covariant period functors to this setting: D_B(V)=(B⊗_{Q_p}V)^{G_K}, comparison α_B:B⊗_{B^{G_K}}D_B(V)→B⊗V. Here B_dR^{G_K}=K and B_cris^{G_K}=B_st^{G_K}=K_0. The associated filtered (φ,N)-module uses Nφ=pφN and the filtration on K⊗D_st induced by B_st→B_dR. Admissibility means α_B is invertible. Contravariant periods are Hom_{Q_p[G_K]}(V,B)=D_B(V^∨). Extend descent data by finite Galois L/K; for the potentially semistable form, use smooth semilinear G_K-actions on finite-dimensional K_0^nr-spaces and filtration on (Kbar⊗D)^{G_K}. The dual filtration is Fil^iD_K^∨=(Fil^{1−i}D_K)^⊥.
hypotheses: V is a finite-dimensional continuous Q_p-representation; K is finite totally ramified over K_0.
With E-coefficients replace the bases by E⊗K and E⊗K_0 and use finite projective modules, not one arbitrarily selected factor.
proofSteps: Use the same period rings and invariant proofs over the perfect-residue base. Apply the regular-period-ring comparison argument. Construct finite descent and the smooth union over finite extensions; define dual structures over the actual coefficient field. This extends the earlier finite-Q_p definitions without a second period carrier.
acceptance: For Q_p(1), D_cris has φ=p^{-1}σ, N=0 and filtration jump −1.
The construction applies to finite extensions of breve Q_p used by Gleason–Lim–Xu.

nodes.title: The fundamental period complex
nodes.statement: For a filtered (φ,N)-module D, define X_st(D)=(B_st⊗D)^{φ=1,N=0}, X_dR(D)=(B_dR⊗D_K)/Fil^0 and C_F(D)=[X_st(D)→X_dR(D)] in degrees 0 and 1, using the fixed period embedding. Its H^0 is V_st(D). Use tensor filtrations, so Fil^0(B_dR⊗D_K)=Σ_i t^{-i}B_dR^+⊗Fil^iD_K. The associated B-pair is (X_st(D),Fil^0(B_dR⊗D_K)); X_dR(D) is its quotient term, not its lattice. For smooth descent data perform the analogous scalar extension over K_0^nr and use D_K=(Kbar⊗D)^{G_K}.
hypotheses: D finite dimensional; φ bijective; N nilpotent; exhaustive separated decreasing filtration; compatible descent data when present.
proofSteps: Construct the comparison map from the invariant subspace to the filtered quotient. Compute the kernel as the intersection of φ=1,N=0 and Fil^0. Apply Colmez–Fontaine §5 exactness of X_st and strict exactness of X_dR. The two terms are topological period modules; finite dimensionality is a conclusion about H^0 under admissibility, not a condition on either term.
acceptance: For admissible D, 0→V_st(D)→X_st(D)→X_dR(D)→0 is exact.

nodes.title: Colmez–Fontaine’s analytic surjectivity lemma
nodes.statement: Let h≥2, V a Q_p-vector space of dimension h, B_2=B_dR^+/t^2, and M a B_2-module of length h with dim_C(tM)=1. Let ξ:V→M be Q_p-linear and assume C⊗V→M/tM is onto. Set U=(B_cris^+)^{φ=p} and ξ_U:U⊗_{Q_p}V→M by u⊗v↦uξ(v). If ker ξ_U is finite-dimensional over Q_p, then ξ_U is onto.
hypotheses: The fixed embedding B_cris^+→B_dR^+ determines multiplication in M; lengths are over B_2.
proofSteps: Choose a basis of V and reduce the image problem to Proposition 2.1’s alternative: a finite-dimensional image from Q_p(1)^h or the full C(1). Prove that alternative using convergent analytic approximations and Newton iteration on the completed integral closure of C{T}. The assumed finite kernel rules out the finite-image alternative; use the surjectivity mod tM to conclude.
acceptance: The hypothesis dim_C tM=1 and the residual surjectivity are both retained; this is not a general Banach open-mapping assertion.

sources.match: The analytic image alternative is proved and applied to this exact module configuration.

nodes.title: The Colmez–Fontaine equivalence
nodes.statement: For K complete discretely valued of mixed characteristic with perfect residue and K finite totally ramified over K_0, every weakly admissible filtered (φ,N)-module D is admissible: dim_{Q_p}V_st(D)=dim_{K_0}D and D_st(V_st(D))≅D. Hence D_st is an exact tensor equivalence from semistable Q_p-representations to weakly admissible filtered (φ,N)-modules, and D_cris is the N=0 specialization. The finite-Galois descent-data version classifies representations of G_K semistable over the chosen extension. No Fontaine–Laffaille, Robba or analytic local-monodromy theorem is a prerequisite.
hypotheses: Weak admissibility means t_H(D)=t_N(D) and t_H(D′)≤t_N(D′) for every φ,N-stable subobject with the induced filtration.
proofSteps: Use the fundamental-complex exactness and Corollary 2.6 to prove Proposition 6.1: neighboring weakly admissible filtrations preserve admissibility. Over algebraically closed residue, reduce to simple slope modules and use §6.2 Lemma 6.4 to find t_h∈(B_cris^+)^{φ^h=p} with θ(t_h)=0. In a cyclic basis, Σ_i φ^i(t_h^s)⊗d_i yields a nonzero V_st for the explicit filtration of slope −s/h. Use length induction, neighboring-filtration chains (Proposition 3.1) and the admissible-subobject criterion (Proposition 4.5) to obtain dimension equality. Descend from the completed maximal unramified base using §6.2 and Proposition 5.4. Recover the exact tensor equivalence from full faithfulness and the dimension criterion; carry finite descent data through the same reconstruction.
acceptance: A line of φ-slope 0 and filtration jump 1 fails weak admissibility and is not reconstructed.
For φe=e,φf=pf and Fil^1=K(e+f), the resulting representation has weights {0,−1} in the convention HT(χ_p)=+1; it does not have weights {0,+1}.

sources.locator: Theorem A and §6.2, pp.1–2,34–35; Proposition 6.1, pp.31–33
sources.match: Gives the independent construction over a perfect residue field and the neighboring-filtration argument.

nodes.title: Locally algebraic coefficient characters
nodes.statement: For finite K,E/Q_p, a continuous character ψ:G_K→E× is locally algebraic when ψ◦Art_K^arith agrees near 1 with the Q_p-points of a morphism Res_{K/Q_p}G_m→Res_{E/Q_p}G_m. If E contains every embedding of K, write this algebraic restriction as ∏_τ τ(x)^{-n_τ}. The integers n_τ are the labeled Hodge–Tate weights, using HT(χ_p)=+1; the corresponding de Rham filtration jumps are −n_τ. Without a splitting coefficient field, the integers are constant on the factor fields of E⊗K, as in Conrad Lemma B.2. Arithmetic and geometric reciprocity give inverse unit characters.
hypotheses: K,E finite over Q_p; Art_K^arith sends a uniformizer to arithmetic Frobenius.
proofSteps: Use the restriction-of-scalars tori and the local reciprocity map from ClassFieldTheory. Over a splitting field classify torus morphisms by integer exponents. Descend exponents along the factor decomposition of E⊗K; compute weights with Lubin–Tate characters and tensor products.
acceptance: Coefficients are retained as an E⊗K-module; no chosen embedding replaces the full labeled tuple.

nodes.title: Rank-one de Rham and crystalline characters
nodes.statement: For a continuous ψ:G_K→E× with K,E finite over Q_p, de Rhamness, Hodge–Tate-ness and local algebraicity are equivalent. The character is crystalline exactly when its algebraic torus morphism agrees with ψ◦Art_K^arith on all O_K×. In that case D_cris(E(ψ)) is invertible over E⊗K_0; if f=[k:F_p] and π is a uniformizer, φ^f acts by ψ(Art_K^arith(π))^{-1}χ_alg(π). The expression is independent of π. In a splitting field the filtration jump at τ is −n_τ. For general E the statement uses all field factors of E⊗K. The description as finite-on-inertia times χ_p^n applies only to parallel Q_p-valued weights.
hypotheses: ψ is continuous; its compact image lies in O_E×; χ_alg is the algebraic part of the preceding definition.
proofSteps: Compute the weight tuple from the algebraic restriction via Lubin–Tate characters. Divide by these crystalline characters: the remainder has finite inertia, so it is potentially unramified and de Rham. Crystalline descent makes the remaining inertia character trivial, proving the all-units condition. Compute φ^f on the Lubin–Tate factors and the unramified factor, then use tensor and coefficient compatibility.
acceptance: A ramified finite-order character is de Rham of weight 0 and is not crystalline.
For an unramified ψ with ψ(Frob_arith)=a, φ^f is a^{-1}.
Nonparallel Lubin–Tate weights rule out a classification by a single cyclotomic power.

sources.locator: Propositions B.3–B.4 and Example B.5, pp.33–36
sources.match: Gives the labeled classification, all-units crystalline criterion and covariant Frobenius formula.

nodes.title: Crystalline lifts of abelian characters
nodes.statement: In the coefficient setup of Böckle–Iyengar–Paškūnas §6, every continuous κ:G_F→O_E× admits a crystalline ψ with ψκ^{-1} trivial on the torsion subgroup of G_F^ab. For a prescribed character χ of μ_{p∞}(F) and residual character κ̄ compatible on their common torsion, ψ can be chosen to lift κ̄ and to have restriction χ. Coefficients may be enlarged to contain the necessary embeddings and roots of unity. A character that is algebraic on O_F× yields a central character with the required algebraic restriction in Lemma 6.6; projectivity of patched modules and existence of deformation components are outgoing applications.
hypotheses: F/Q_p finite; coefficient field and roots of unity as in the source’s §6; prescribed residual and p-power torsion restrictions agree.
proofSteps: Use local class field theory to split uniformizer, residue-unit torsion and principal-unit factors. Choose integer exponents of embedding characters to realize the torsion restrictions and residual unit character, with the source’s congruence conditions. Extend the all-units algebraic character by a unit-valued uniformizer character and apply the rank-one crystalline criterion.
acceptance: Incompatible residual and p-power torsion restrictions cannot be prescribed simultaneously.

sources.match: Produces crystalline characters with torsion and residual constraints and applies algebraicity to the central character.

nodes.title: Regular ordinary coefficient representations
nodes.statement: Let E contain every embedding τ:K→E and λ_τ=(λ_{τ,1}≥⋯≥λ_{τ,n}) be integral dominant weights. Put h_{τ,i}=λ_{τ,i}+n−i. A representation V:G_K→GL_n(E) is ordinary of weight λ when it admits a decreasing G_K-stable full flag with one-dimensional graded characters χ_i satisfying χ_i◦Art_K^geom(x)=∏_τ τ(x)^{-h_{τ,i}} for x in an open subgroup of O_K×. Equivalently the increasing flag orders the characters in reverse, so its i-th exponent is −(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1). With HT(χ_p)=+1 the weights of χ_i are −h_{τ,i}. This regular, embedding-labeled definition is distinct from the Perrin–Riou parallel cyclotomic filtration of R06.4.
hypotheses: K,E finite over Q_p; E splits the embeddings; geometric reciprocity sends a uniformizer to geometric Frobenius; every h_{τ,i}>h_{τ,i+1}.
proofSteps: Build the full stable flag and attach its locally algebraic rank-one quotients. Compare decreasing and increasing indexing by i↦n−i+1; convert reciprocity using inversion. Use the character classification to compute the weight tuple of each graded piece.
acceptance: No equality on all units is imposed for ordinarity; finite-order inertia factors are allowed.

sources.locator: conventions, p.6; ordinarity definition and Lemma 2.2, pp.17–18
sources.match: Defines the decreasing ordinary flag and its labeled characters using geometric reciprocity.
Uses the increasing upper-triangular form with the reversed weight indexing.

nodes.title: Frobenius and maximal-monodromy ordinarity
nodes.statement: For a crystalline V of regular weight λ in the preceding convention, let α_1,…,α_n be eigenvalues of φ^f on D_cris(V), ordered by decreasing valuation. Normalize v_K(p)=e_K. Then V is ordinary of weight λ if and only if v_K(α_i)=Σ_τ h_{τ,i} for every i; equivalently v_p(α_i)=e_K^{-1}Σ_τ h_{τ,i}. A semistable representation with dim ker N^j=j for 1≤j≤n−1 and, at every τ, filtration jumps exactly 0,1,…,n−1 is ordinary of weight 0. The second clause does not assert ordinarity for arbitrary regular filtration jumps.
hypotheses: The eigenvalues are computed after an adequate finite coefficient extension; D_cris is the covariant period module; f is the residue degree.
proofSteps: For the crystalline case compare Newton and Hodge polygons. Equality at every break forces each Frobenius subspace in the ordered flag to be weakly admissible with the induced filtration. Reconstruct the stable characters by Colmez–Fontaine and use rank-one weights; conversely compute slopes from the ordinary flag. For maximal monodromy use the nested kernels of N and weak admissibility with exactly the consecutive source jumps.
acceptance: The normalization has an e_K factor but no extra f factor when summing over every embedding τ.
Maximal N with nonconsecutive regular weights is not covered by the second clause.

sources.match: Supplies the slope criterion and the consecutive-weight maximal-monodromy case.

nodes.title: Finite-extension descent of regular ordinarity
nodes.statement: Let V be a regular de Rham E-representation of G_K, with its labeled weights obtained from λ as above, and L/K finite. If V|_{G_L} is ordinary with the weights restricted along embeddings of L, then V is ordinary of weight λ. Coefficient extension has the same descent property. The regular hypothesis distinguishes successive characters by their labeled weights; mere triangularity after extension does not imply a stable flag over K.
hypotheses: K,L,E finite over Q_p; E can be enlarged to split all relevant embeddings; λ is regular at every embedding.
proofSteps: Use the strictly ordered labeled weights to characterize the ordinary flag and its successive ranks intrinsically. Pass to a Galois extension and conjugate the flag; uniqueness makes it G_K-stable. Descend its coefficient subspaces and convert the character restrictions by local reciprocity.
acceptance: The proof must establish uniqueness of the regular ordinary flag before using Galois descent.

sources.locator: Definition 1.2, PDF p.2; descent is the target deduction described here
sources.match: Defines the regular ordinary flag; the finite-extension descent conclusion is a target deduction, with the indicated regular-flag uniqueness hypothesis.

nodes.title: Crystalline representations with G-structure
nodes.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected reductive, K a finite extension of breve Q_p, b∈G(breve Q_p) and μ:G_m→G_K a K-defined cocharacter. Define F_{b,μ}:Rep_{Q_p}(G)→FilIsoc_K by ρ↦(V⊗breve Q_p,ρ(b)σ,Fil_μ), where Fil_μ^i is the sum of the μ-weight spaces of weights ≥i. Call (b,μ) admissible when this object is weakly admissible for every algebraic ρ. Colmez–Fontaine then defines an exact Q_p-linear tensor functor V_cris◦F_{b,μ} to crystalline G_K-representations. Its underlying vector-space functor ω_{b,μ} has an Isom^⊗(ω_std,ω_{b,μ}) G-torsor; choosing a Q_p-point identifies it with a conjugacy class of representations G_K→G(Q_p).
hypotheses: K/breve Q_p finite; μ is defined over K rather than merely an abstract conjugacy class; every ρ is finite dimensional.
proofSteps: Apply every algebraic representation to b and μ. Verify tensor, dual and exact compatibility of weight filtrations, then test weak admissibility representationwise. Apply the N=0 Colmez–Fontaine equivalence. Use the shared Tannakian reconstruction theorem to form the torsor; a chosen tensor isomorphism transfers the G_K-action.
acceptance: Admissibility alone produces a G-torsor; it is not a canonical choice of a homomorphism into G(Q_p).

nodes.title: Fixed-bound triviality of the crystalline torsor
nodes.statement: For the admissible pair above, assume the σ-conjugacy class [b] lies in B(G,{μ}), with its Newton bound and Kottwitz invariant both matching {μ}. Then Isom^⊗(ω_std,ω_{b,μ}) has a Q_p-point. Thus the crystalline realization determines a G(Q_p)-conjugacy class ξ_{b,μ}:G_K→G(Q_p). No triviality is asserted for arbitrary admissible pairs without the fixed-bound condition.
hypotheses: G connected reductive over Q_p; K/breve Q_p finite; μ is K-defined and (b,μ) is admissible.
proofSteps: Compute the torsor’s Kottwitz class via the filtered isocrystal tensor functor and identify its obstruction with the difference between the Newton/Kottwitz data of b and the Hodge type μ. Apply the fixed-bound vanishing theorem quoted in GLX. Prove the obstruction vanishing at the specified bound.
acceptance: For G=GL_n the conclusion agrees with Hilbert 90; the theorem is also required for nonspecial G.

sources.match: Uses the fixed-bound condition to produce a G(Q_p)-valued crystalline homomorphism.

nodes.title: Crystalline monodromy and Tannakian groups
nodes.statement: After a tensor trivialization, let H be the Zariski closure of ξ_{b,μ}(G_K) in G and set MT=H^∘. The tensor subcategory generated by the realized algebraic representations and closed under subquotients has full Tannakian group H for its forgetful fiber functor. Its connected group after restriction to a finite extension killing H/H^∘ is MT. Changing trivialization conjugates both. The image contains an open subgroup of MT(Q_p). For a sufficiently large decent unramified coefficient field, the corresponding crystalline Tannakian group and MT become pure inner forms under the same connectedness convention.
hypotheses: Use an admissible fixed-bound pair and specify whether the full or connected monodromy category is meant.
proofSteps: Use Tannakian reconstruction for the full algebraic closure H. Kill its finite component group by an open subgroup of G_K before taking MT. Apply the crystalline open-image and comparison statements invoked by GLX; record their external primary-proof requirement.
acceptance: A finite nontrivial image has H finite and MT=1; the full tensor category does not have group MT.

sources.match: Defines the connected closure, invokes open image, and compares the crystalline fiber functor.

nodes.title: Harder–Narasimhan structure of filtered isocrystals
nodes.statement: For a nonzero filtered (φ,N)-module D define rk(D)=dim D, deg(D)=t_H(D)−t_N(D) and μ(D)=deg(D)/rk(D), with the analogous smooth-descent version. An induced subobject is a φ,N-stable subspace with its induced filtration. Semistability means every nonzero induced subobject has slope ≤μ(D). Define the unique strict Harder–Narasimhan filtration with decreasing semistable slopes, and call D acyclic when all its HN slopes are ≥0. Weak admissibility is exactly semistability of slope 0. Duality reverses and negates the slope list. The tensor product uses the convolution filtration and diagonal operators; its slope statement is part of the HN tensor interface.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional filtered modules with exhaustive separated filtrations; use t_N normalized by v_p and the actual coefficient field for the dual.
proofSteps: Use rank and degree additivity in strict exact sequences and the finite-dimensional subobject slope bound to construct the maximal-slope subobject and induct on rank. Prove uniqueness from the slope inequality for morphisms. Identify slope-zero semistability with the weak-admissibility inequalities. Use the filtered-isocrystal tensor theorem for tensor slopes; this requires the filtered-isocrystal tensor theorem at arbitrary slopes.
acceptance: A line φ=p^aσ and filtration jump b has degree b−a and slope b−a.

sources.match: Uses the HN structure, weak admissibility and acyclicity; its degree sign is corrected by its slope inequalities.
