nodes.title: Contravariant periods on almost C-representations
nodes.statement: For W in the shared category C(G_K) of almost C-representations, define D_st^*(W)=Hom_{G_K,cont}(W,B_st), D_dR^*(W)=Hom_{G_K,cont}(W,B_dR), with Fil^i consisting of maps whose image lies in t^iB_dR^+, and D_pst^*(W)=colim_{L/K finite}Hom_{G_L,cont}(W,B_st). Frobenius and monodromy act on values. The last object has smooth semilinear G_K-action over K_0^nr. These modules are finite dimensional and the natural scalar-extended maps into D_dR^* are injective. On finite-dimensional Q_p-representations they recover D_B(V^∨). The covariant tensor-invariant formula is not a finite-dimensional extension to all almost C-representations.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued with perfect residue, countable as in CN; W is an object of the shared almost C-category with its topology.
proofSteps: Import the actual almost C-category and its finite-dimensional presentation, rather than identify it with finite-dimensional C-spaces. Use Hom_{G_K,cont}(C,B_dR)=0 to remove the C-part of a presentation. This gives finite-dimensionality; use the injective K⊗B_st→B_dR comparison for the natural maps. Take the smooth union for potential periods.
acceptance: For W=C, all three contravariant period modules vanish.

sources.match: Extends the contravariant period functors and proves finiteness by vanishing on C.

nodes.title: Contravariant reconstruction for acyclic modules
nodes.statement: For an acyclic filtered (φ,N)-module D, V=H^0C_F(D) is an almost C-representation and X_st(D)→X_dR(D) is onto. The natural pairings identify D_st^*(V)=D^∨ and D_dR^*(V)=(D_K^∨,Fil_⊥). With smooth descent, D_pst^*(V)=D^∨. In the slope-zero case V is finite dimensional and this recovers Colmez–Fontaine. For nonzero nonnegative slopes V need not be a finite-dimensional Q_p-representation.
hypotheses: HN slopes are nonnegative; use the shared almost C-category and the fixed B_st→B_dR embedding.
proofSteps: Prove the local analytic surjectivity of X_st(D)→X_dR(D) for the nonnegative filtered HN slopes. The equivalent field-curve calculation gives H^1=0; its equivariant topological period realization must be identified.

Construct an admissible subfiltration of the same D and realize the quotient by finite t-adic interval modules, as in Colmez–Nizioł (5.6). Prove the continuous-Hom vanishing for these quotients, then use period bounds for the finite-dimensional admissible kernel.

Identify the dual filtration by Fil^0(B_dR⊗D_K)=Σ_i t^{-i}B_dR^+⊗Fil^iD_K and descend the smooth Galois structure. This gives the contravariant period reconstructions and their covariance under tensor duality.
acceptance: For the slope-zero unit D this gives the ordinary finite-dimensional fundamental exact sequence.
Reconstruction gives D_K^∨, not D_K, in the contravariant functor.

sources.locator: Remark 5.5 with (5.6), pp.33–34; Theorem 5.8 and Corollary 5.9, pp.34–35
sources.match: Proves contravariant reconstruction using the admissible subfiltration and vanishing on t-adic quotients.

nodes.title: Coefficient B-pairs and strict morphisms
nodes.statement: For K,E/Q_p finite let B_e=B_cris^{φ=1}. An E-B-pair W consists of a finite free (B_e⊗E)-module W_e with continuous semilinear G_K-action and a G_K-stable finite free (B_dR^+⊗E)-lattice W_dR^+ in W_dR=B_dR⊗_{B_e}W_e. Both have the same E-rank. A morphism has compatible equivariant linear maps on both components agreeing after B_dR extension. It is strict when the cokernel of its lattice map is torsion free over B_dR^+⊗E. Exact sequences use strict maps; the category of B-pairs is not abelian. Tensor products and duals are componentwise. A modification changes the lattice while retaining W_e. W(V)=(B_e⊗V,B_dR^+⊗V), and W(D)=((B_st⊗D)^{φ=1,N=0},Fil^0(B_dR⊗D_K)).
hypotheses: Coefficient tensor products retain the complete E-algebra, rather than one scalar factor; all actions have the natural period topology.
proofSteps: Use the existing period rings and their comparison embeddings. Specify free modules, the common scalar extension and a full lattice. Define componentwise morphisms and restrict exactness to torsion-free lattice quotients. Extend Berger’s Q_p formulation by the E-action and use Nakamura’s coefficient definition.
acceptance: The quotient B_dR/W_dR^+ is not the lattice component.

sources.match: Defines the two components, strict exactness, modifications and the classical examples.
Retains E-coefficients and the period-module lattice data.

Attaches a genuine lattice to the fundamental period data.

nodes.title: Berger’s B-pair–Robba equivalence
nodes.statement: The category of E-B-pairs is tensor equivalent to finite free (φ,Γ_K)-modules over the coefficient Robba ring. For W, its extended module consists of y in B̃_rig^†[1/t]⊗_{B_e}W_e whose images under every sufficiently large localization ι_n lie in W_dR^+. Descent gives D(W). Conversely W_e(D)=(B̃_rig^†[1/t]⊗D)^{φ=1} and W_dR^+(D)=B_dR^+⊗_{ι_n}D^{r_n} for n large; the latter is independent of n. These constructions are mutually inverse, preserve strict exact sequences and identify W(V) with D_rig^†(V). The pairs arising from representations correspond precisely to étale modules. A modification corresponds to an isomorphism after inverting t.
hypotheses: Use radii and localization maps on the shared Robba carriers; coefficient E-actions commute with φ,Γ_K.
proofSteps: Impose the lattice condition simultaneously at every large cyclotomic localization. Prove finite freeness over the extended Robba ring by elementary divisors and control of all localization ideals. Use Tate–Sen descent and annulus gluing to descend the extended module. Construct the reverse e-invariants and lattice, prove its stability for increasing n, and compare both scalar extensions to obtain inverse functors. Apply the shared slope-zero criterion for the representation subcategory.
acceptance: Multiplying the lattice by t^m replaces D(W) by t^mD(W).
The equivalence is for all B-pairs, but only slope-zero pairs come from Galois representations.

sources.locator: Lemmas 2.2.1–2.2.2, Propositions 2.2.4–2.2.6, Theorem 2.2.7 and Proposition 2.2.9, pp.13–17
sources.match: Builds the two functors, proves descent, and identifies the étale subcategory.

nodes.title: Cohomology of B-pairs through Robba modules
nodes.statement: Transport the shared Herr cohomology of D(W) to an E-B-pair W. The cohomology is finite dimensional, concentrated in degrees 0,1,2, and χ(W)=−[K:Q_p]rk_E(W). Cup product and trace induce perfect pairings H^i(W)×H^{2−i}(W^∨(1))→E. For W(V) these are the continuous G_K-cohomology groups and their Tate pairings. The complex, cup product and trace are the shared P7 Herr interface.
hypotheses: K,E finite over Q_p; W an E-B-pair; the source Q_p results are extended by the finite coefficient action.
proofSteps: Apply Berger’s equivalence and import Liu’s Herr cohomology, Euler characteristic and duality. Verify that W(V) maps to the étale module in Liu Theorem 0.1 and that tensor duality preserves the cyclotomic dualizing object.
acceptance: For rank one and K=Q_p the Euler characteristic is −1, independent of its slope.

sources.match: Identifies Galois cohomology on the étale subcategory and proves Euler characteristic and perfect duality for all Robba modules.

nodes.title: Coefficient de Rham period representations
nodes.statement: A B_dR-representation of G_K is a finite-dimensional B_dR-vector space with continuous semilinear G_K-action. An E-coefficient representation is a finite free B_dR⊗E-module with commuting E-action. A stable positive lattice is a finite free B_dR^+⊗E-submodule spanning it after inversion of t. Put D_dR(W)=W^{G_K}; the representation is de Rham when the scalar-extension map B_dR⊗_K D_dR(W)→W is invertible. A stable lattice induces Fil^iD_dR(W)=D_dR(W)∩t^iW_dR^+. If E contains all K-embeddings, group the coefficient decomposition by σ:K→E as W_dR^+=⊕_σ W_dR,σ^+, over B_dR^+⊗_{K,σ}E; each factor retains its E-algebra structure and rank.
hypotheses: K,E finite over Q_p for Fontaine’s classification; the coefficient σ-components are not asserted to be fields.
proofSteps: Use finite free period modules and the actual topological semilinear action. Define the comparison map and lattice-intersection filtration. Decompose E⊗K by K-embeddings and transport this decomposition to the coefficient period module.
acceptance: A stable lattice is extra data: the B_dR-representation alone does not determine its integer filtration jumps.

sources.match: Uses semilinear B_dR-representations and their stable positive lattices.
Defines and groups coefficient de Rham lattices by the embeddings σ.

nodes.title: Fontaine’s de Rham representation classification
nodes.statement: For K/Q_p finite, the simple continuous semilinear B_dR-representations are indexed by G_K-orbits a in Kbar/Z. For a chosen lift A in Kbar, let D_a be the associated endomorphism division algebra with center K_a, [D_a:K_a]=p^{2s_a}, and d_a=[K_a:K]. The simple B_dR[a] has dimension d_ap^{s_a}; changing the lift by an integer gives an isomorphic simple. The indecomposables are B_dR[a;d]=B_dR[a]⊗_{Z_p}Z_p(0;d), where d≥1 and Z_p(0;d) is Fontaine’s logarithmic unipotent block. Every B_dR-representation has a unique finite decomposition into these blocks with multiplicities. An E-action is retained by passing to modules with commuting E-action; it is not discarded by the classification. The trivial de Rham objects are sums of B_dR, whereas almost de Rham logarithmic blocks need not be trivial.
hypotheses: The Sen-block notation D_a,K_a,s_a,d_a and Z_p(0;d) is defined by the Sen classification and logarithmic unipotent representation in Fontaine §§2.6 and 3.2.
proofSteps: Apply Fontaine’s decompletion to regular-singular K_∞((t))-connections. Reduce their semisimple blocks to the Sen representation classification; integer shifts are removed by multiplication by t. Identify the indecomposable logarithmic extensions and use their division-algebra endomorphisms and Krull–Schmidt uniqueness. Keep any commuting E-action throughout.
acceptance: B_dR(χ_p^m)≅B_dR by a t-power, although a fixed positive lattice retains its integer jump.
B_dR[0;2] is indecomposable and almost de Rham but not the trivial rank-two representation.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.18 and Theorem 3.19, pp.67–68; paragraph after Theorem 3.19, p.69
sources.match: Classifies simples and indecomposables with their division-algebra dimensions and unique multiplicities.

nodes.title: Embedding-selective de Rham lattice modification
nodes.statement: In Ding Proposition 2.5’s generic noncritical crystabelline rank-n setup, fix σ:K→E and strictly decreasing labeled weights h_{τ,1}>⋯>h_{τ,n}, using HT(χ_p)=+1. Define an E-B-pair W_σ with the same e-component as W(D) and the same σ-component of W_dR^+. For τ≠σ, replace its lattice by t^{h_{τ,n}}(B_dR^+⊗_{K,τ}E)^n inside the common trivialized de Rham component. Berger’s equivalence gives D_σ with D⊂D_σ, D[1/t]=D_σ[1/t], D_pst(D)=D_pst(D_σ), and the σ-filtered de Rham components agree. At each other τ all weights become h_{τ,n}. This is the local period modification; deformation spaces and critical-type local models remain with their owners.
hypotheses: Use all generic/noncritical crystabelline hypotheses of Ding Proposition 2.5 and a common de Rham trivialization; the minimum-weight lattice contains the original.
proofSteps: Keep the e-part and σ-lattice, replace the other positive lattices by the displayed homotheties, and check G_K-stability. Use Fontaine’s de Rham representation and lattice description for the coefficient components. Apply Berger’s modification equivalence and invariance of the e-period functors to obtain D_σ.
acceptance: For [K:Q_p]=1 and σ its sole embedding, D_σ=D.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.5 and its proof, pp.13–14; §2.1, pp.9–10
sources.match: Constructs the one-embedding modification and proves its period invariance, invoking Fontaine Theorem 3.19.

nodes.title: Primitive comparison and proper smooth finiteness
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p and X a proper smooth rigid adic space over Spa(C,O_C). For every finite locally constant F_p-sheaf L, H^i_et(X,L) is finite dimensional, vanishes for i>2dim X, and the natural map H^i_et(X,L)⊗_{F_p}O_C/p→H^i_et(X,L⊗O_X^+/p) is an almost isomorphism. The almost ideal is the maximal ideal of O_C; the same statement holds on the pro-étale site. For a finite free lisse Z_p-sheaf T, H^i_et(X,T) is a finite Z_p-module; the corresponding rational primitive map H^i_et(X,T)⊗C→H^i_proet(X,T⊗Ô_X) is an isomorphism. For X descending to a proper smooth space over a complete discretely valued K, the positive period map H^i_et(X,T)⊗B_dR^+→H^i_proet(X,T⊗B_dR^+) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Proper and smooth are both imposed; L is finite locally constant. Integral comparison is almost, not an ordinary isomorphism.
proofSteps: Cover X by nested finite collections of small toric affinoids. Use the perfectoid root towers, almost acyclicity and continuous Z_p^d-cohomology to obtain almost finite generation of the restriction images; pass through the finite Čech spectral sequence. Apply the tilted inverse-limit freeness lemma to cohomology and use the tilted Artin–Schreier sequence to identify its Frobenius fixed part with finite F_p-cohomology. Devissage gives finite p-power coefficients, the inverse-limit theorem gives finite Z_p-cohomology, and inversion of p kills almost errors. For B_dR^+ use its filtered quotients, gr^j=Ô_X(j), finite-coefficient primitive comparison and controlled inverse limits as in Scholze Theorem 8.4. The argument uses the perfectoid and almost section calculations directly.
acceptance: For X=Spa(C,O_C), H^0(F_p)=F_p and all higher finite-constant cohomology vanishes.
For P^1_C, H^0 and H^2(F_p) have dimension 1 and H^1=0.
An arbitrary nonproper smooth affinoid is not covered by the finiteness conclusion.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.1, pp.28–29; Lemmas 5.6 and 5.8–5.10 and proof, pp.31–34; Theorem 8.4 and proof, pp.48–50
sources.match: Proves the early almost primitive theorem by finite covers and tilted Artin–Schreier, then the positive-period comparison.

nodes.title: Étale–pro-étale cohomology and base change
nodes.statement: Let ν:X_proet→X_et for a locally noetherian adic space. For an abelian étale sheaf F, F→Rν_*ν^*F is invertible. In particular étale and pro-étale cohomology agree for F_p-local systems and for the uncompleted étale sheaf O_X^+/p pulled back by ν. If f:X→Y is qcqs, ν_Y^*Rf_et*F→Rf_proet*ν_X^*F is invertible. For qcqs U=lim_jU_j in X_proet, H^i(U,ν^*F)=colim_jH^i(U_j,F). The assertion does not identify a completed integral sheaf with its uncompleted pullback in every topology.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian spaces and qcqs f or U where stated; F is an étale sheaf before pullback.
proofSteps: Compute an injective étale sheaf on inverse limits of qcqs étale objects. Reduce finite pro-étale covers to finite-stage étale covers and pass their Čech complexes through filtered colimits. This proves the cohomology formula, the adjunction and the proper base-change map by sheafification.
acceptance: The statement applies to ν^*(O_X^+/p), and completion is handled separately by the local-acyclicity theorem.

sources.match: Computes the cohomology of pulled-back étale sheaves and the qcqs base-change map.

nodes.title: Relative primitive comparison
nodes.statement: For a proper smooth morphism f:X→S of locally noetherian adic spaces over Q_p and a finite F_p-local system L, (R^if_et*L)⊗O_S^{+a}/p→R^if_et*(L⊗O_X^{+a}/p) is an almost isomorphism. On the pro-étale site, if the finite-coefficient direct images of a finite free lisse Z_p-sheaf T are locally constant finite modules with the required inverse-limit control, R^if_*T⊗Ô_S→R^if_*(T⊗Ô_X) is an isomorphism. In particular R^if_*Ẑ_p⊗Ô_S≅R^if_*Ô_X under the local-freeness hypothesis on every R^if_*F_p used by Caraiani–Scholze.
hypotheses: The almost ideal is the sheaf of locally topologically nilpotent elements. The rational statement retains the finite-coefficient local-freeness and limit hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply absolute primitive comparison at conservative geometric pro-étale fibers and proper base change. Use étale–pro-étale agreement to transport the finite-coefficient map. Pass through p-power devissage and controlled inverse limits and invert p.
acceptance: For f the identity, the comparison is the scalar-extension identity.
Geometric fiberwise comparison alone does not justify an uncontrolled inverse limit.

sources.match: Gives the relative almost primitive theorem and the lisse-relative comparison hypotheses.
Uses the primitive completed-structure comparison under finite-coefficient local freeness.

nodes.title: Geometric Hodge–Tate direct images
nodes.statement: For X smooth over a complete algebraically closed extension C/Q_p and ν:X_proet→X_et, R^nν_*Ô_X is canonically Ω_X^n(−n), compatible with exterior cup products and étale pullback. These sheaves are coherent, vanish for n>dim X, and R^0ν_*Ô_X=O_X. This is a geometric statement. Over a discretely valued arithmetic base K the extra log χ row in R^iν_*Ô_X(j) must be retained; the geometric formula does not erase it before base change.
hypotheses: X is smooth; Ω_X is the analytic coherent differential sheaf over C.
proofSteps: On a toric chart compute continuous Z_p^d-cohomology of the perfectoid root tower and identify degree-one Kummer classes with dlog coordinates. Cup products identify higher degrees with exterior powers. Descend across étale chart changes using the intrinsic boundary of the Faltings extension, then sheafify. BMS’s integral Lη calculation agrees after inversion of p.

For arbitrary C, use Scholze survey Lemma 3.24: approximate coefficients by smooth finite-type Q_p-algebras, descend finite étale charts to a finite stage, and compare Faltings boundary maps. The boundedness of both maps on integral units and approximation modulo p^m establish Kummer compatibility independently of coordinates. Constants from the auxiliary base admit compatible p-power roots in C, so their boundary classes vanish. Exterior cup products give the higher-degree identifications.
acceptance: For a one-dimensional torus, R^1ν_*Ô=O·dlog T(−1) and all R^n for n>1 vanish.
Over K, the arithmetic log χ contribution provides a test distinguishing the two bases.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.16 and its proof, pp.39–41; Corollary 6.19, p.41
sources.match: Computes toric perfectoid cohomology and the intrinsic degree-one boundary; arithmetic invariants give the additional row.

sources.locator: Theorem 8.3 and Theorem 8.7, pp.61–63; Proposition 8.9, p.63
sources.match: Provides the compatible integral toric calculation, whose rationalization is the geometric direct-image formula.
The all-C direct-image formula is proved by toric covers and intrinsic Kummer dlog descent; all exterior powers are included.

nodes.title: Fundamental crystalline period-sheaf sequences
nodes.statement: In Tan–Tong’s absolutely unramified smooth formal-model setting, with the pro-étale crystalline sheaves and their completed filtration, the map 1−φ gives an exact sequence 0→Q_p→Fil^0B_cris→B_cris→0. Multiplication by t^r gives 0→Q_p(r)→Fil^rB_cris→B_cris→0 with map 1−p^{−r}φ for every integer r. The scalar sequence 0→Q_p→B_cris^{φ=1}→B_dR/B_dR^+→0 holds at the arithmetic geometric point. Its proposed sheaf analogue requires a separate local lifting proof and is not inferred from scalar exactness.
hypotheses: Fix the map B_cris→B_dR and the chosen cyclotomic t; retain the source’s base restrictions for structural crystalline periods.
proofSteps: Use the scalar fundamental sequences on geometric fibers and solve the Frobenius equation pro-étale locally on perfectoid objects. Check that the filtered image in the de Rham quotient is independent of the local generator. Use the exactness theorem of Tan–Tong for the stated unramified structural setting.
acceptance: At a geometric point these are the scalar Fontaine sequences.
The arrows form two short exact sequences; they are not one sequence obtained by concatenating their middle terms.

sources.match: The filtered fundamental exact sequence is stated for the absolutely unramified formal-model period sheaves.
The relative scalar invariant-to-quotient fundamental sequence is proved by the filtered Frobenius calculation.

nodes.title: Relative Hodge–Tate filtration
nodes.statement: For a proper smooth π:X→S of smooth adic spaces over a complete discretely valued K with perfect residue, assume every R^iπ_*F_p is locally free. Put H=R^iπ_dR*O_X with Hodge filtration and Gauss–Manin connection, M=R^iπ_*Ẑ_p⊗B_dR,S^+ and M_0=(H⊗O_S OB_dR,S^+)^{∇=0}, where M_0 uses the trivial filtration on H. Relative comparison identifies M[1/t]=M_0[1/t]. In this ambient module M_0⊂M. Define the ascending filtration on M/tM by F_{−j}=(M∩t^jM_0)/(tM∩t^jM_0). Its graded piece gr_F^j(M/tM)=gr_Hodge^jH⊗Ô_S(−j), F_{−1}=0 and F_i=M/tM. Before reduction, (M∩t^jM_0)/(M∩t^{j+1}M_0)=Fil_Hodge^{−j}H⊗Ô_S(j).
hypotheses: π proper smooth; X,S smooth; every finite-coefficient direct image locally free. OB_dR^+ is the corrected completed structural sheaf.
proofSteps: Apply the existing corrected local Poincaré lemma and relative comparison to identify the two lattices in the same B_dR module. Use the lattice-filtration position theorem to compute their intersections. Reduce by tM to obtain an ascending filtration and compute its graded terms from the Hodge filtration.
acceptance: The inclusion direction is M_0⊂M and the graded twist is −j.

sources.match: Describes the two lattices, their intersections, ascending filtration and graded twists.
Requires integral completion before inversion of p in the structural sheaf.

nodes.title: The natural first Hodge–Tate step
nodes.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, F_0 on R^iπ_*Ẑ_p⊗Ô_S is the image of the natural injective map R^iπ_*O_X⊗Ô_S→R^iπ_*Ô_X≅R^iπ_*Ẑ_p⊗Ô_S. The map is induced by O_X→Ô_X and the primitive comparison; it is not chosen from a splitting of the graded pieces. Associated tensor and dual constructions preserve the filtration by their tensor and dual rules.
hypotheses: Use the fixed relative comparison and corrected OB_dR^+.
proofSteps: Extend M_0→M to structural periods. The relative Poincaré lemma identifies this map with the inclusion O_X→OB_dR,X^+. Reduce the complex modulo Fil^1; it becomes O_X→Ô_X. The lattice-intersection graded formula shows that the image has the expected rank and that the natural map is injective. Tensor compatibility is inherited from the associated filtered flat bundle functor.
acceptance: For an abelian family, this is the H^1(O) subbundle; the full degree-one specialization belongs to T1.

sources.match: Identifies F_0 by the natural structure-sheaf map instead of a splitting.

nodes.title: Associated de Rham pairs
nodes.statement: For X smooth over a finite extension K/Q_p, an associated de Rham pair consists of a finite-rank Q_p-local system L, a filtered vector bundle (E,∇,Fil) with integrable Griffiths-transversal connection, and an isomorphism L⊗OB_dR≅E⊗OB_dR respecting connection and tensor filtration. Equivalently L⊗B_dR^+≅M(E), compatibly after structural extension. Association is data; being de Rham means such data exist. Morphisms respect both components and the isomorphism. Tensor products use convolution filtration; duals use Fil^iE^∨=(Fil^{1−i}E)^⊥. The filtered flat bundle functor M is fully faithful, but its essential image is the associated lattices, not every B_dR^+-local system.
hypotheses: Use the corrected structural period sheaf and finite, locally split, exhaustive separated filtration. A Q_p-local system is allowed to have lattices only locally, as in Shimizu Definition 8.2.
proofSteps: Use the existing M construction and horizontal Poincaré equivalence. Take Fil^0 of the comparison and horizontal sections to obtain the lattice isomorphism. Conversely extend it to OB_dR with the induced filtration and connection. Recover morphisms from horizontal maps and the filtration-position theorem.
acceptance: Changing a Q_p-lattice leaves the rational associated pair unchanged.

sources.locator: Definition 7.4, Theorem 7.6 and Proposition 7.9, pp.42–45; Definition 8.3, pp.48–49
sources.match: Defines filtered flat bundles, the fully faithful association functor and the de Rham local-system condition.
Restates the functor with Griffiths transversality and distinguishes its source from arbitrary period local systems.
Uses rational local systems defined by locally available lattices.

nodes.title: Period local systems on rigid spaces and diamonds
nodes.statement: For X smooth over a p-adic field K, the category of finite-rank B_dR^+-local systems on X_proet is canonically equivalent to that on the associated locally spatial diamond X^diamond. On an affinoid perfectoid toric cover U=Spa(A,A^+), both categories are finite projective B_dR^+(A)-modules; the equivalence identifies continuous semilinear descent and preserves tensor products, duals, t-inversion and reduction modulo t. It sends M(E) to the same period lattice on the diamond.
hypotheses: Diamond period local systems use the period sheaf on the v-site and the descent convention of Howe–Klevdal §2.3.
proofSteps: Choose toric charts and their cyclotomic root towers. Use finite-projective descent on the perfectoid cover. Compare the same continuous semilinear action of Z_p(1)^n⋊Z_p^×, and then the étale descent between charts. This constructs the equivalence and its tensor compatibility.
acceptance: A finite projective module need not have a chosen free basis globally.

sources.match: Gives the perfectoid-cover and descent-data proof and cites Scholze–Weinstein Corollary 17.1.9.
Finite-projective B_dR^+ modules satisfy v-descent, and the category on an affinoid perfectoid is recovered from its period ring.

nodes.title: Horizontal relative periods
nodes.statement: Let K be finite totally ramified over Frac W(k), k perfect. Let R satisfy Shimizu Set-up 3.1: R is a normal domain finite flat over a p-adically completed toric base obtained by étale extensions, localizations and completions; R[1/p] is étale over that base, K is algebraically closed in R[1/p], its reduced special fiber is geometrically integral, and the stated geometrically regular-fiber or dimension<2 condition holds. Write Rbar for the union of finite normal extensions étale after inverting p and Rhat for its p-adic completion. Evaluate the shared relative period constructions on (Rhat[1/p],Rhat). Define B_max^∇, B_cris^∇ and B_dR^∇ by these evaluations. Define B_st^∇=B_max^∇[u] embedded by u↦log([p^flat]/p), with φ(u)=pu and N=−d/du. For V a continuous Q_p-representation of G_{R[1/p]}, set D_B^∇(V)=(B^∇⊗V)^G and its multiplication comparison. Horizontal crystalline, semistable or de Rham means that comparison is invertible for B_max^∇, B_st^∇ or B_dR^∇. Horizontal crystalline can equivalently use B_cris^∇. The invariant bases are K_0,K_0,K respectively; (B_st^∇)^{N=0}=B_max^∇. Condition (BR) means R equals its smooth toric base and is imposed for the crystalline/semistable dual and monodromy theorems.
hypotheses: A common root system and logarithm embedding is fixed; root changes add an element of B_max^∇ and transport all structures.
proofSteps: Evaluate the shared θ-completion and PD constructions; the max construction adjoins ker θ/p before p-adic completion. Use the logarithm transcendence theorem to identify the semistable ring with a polynomial algebra over B_max, rather than over B_cris. Apply invariant and injectivity theorems to prove the dimension criterion.
acceptance: The structural period ring with connection is not substituted for the horizontal evaluation ring.

sources.locator: Set-up 3.1 and Definition 3.2, pp.18–19; Definitions 2.25–2.38, pp.13–16; Definitions 4.7 and 4.16, Lemmas 4.14–4.19, pp.22–25
sources.match: Specifies the base rings, horizontal period carriers, comparison definition, max/crystalline equivalence and dual restrictions.

nodes.title: Local monodromy for de Rham local systems
nodes.statement: For R satisfying the preceding set-up and BR, every horizontal de Rham representation becomes horizontal semistable after a finite extension L/K; if one classical specialization is potentially crystalline, L can be chosen to make it horizontal crystalline. Consequently, for a de Rham Q_p-local system on a smooth quasi-separated rigid space X/K and a classical point x, there is an open neighborhood U of x in X_{k(x)} and a finite extension L/k(x) such that the restriction to U_L is horizontal de Rham and semistable at every classical point. If its stalk at x is potentially crystalline, all those stalks can be chosen crystalline. For qc X a single finite L/K makes all K-rational stalks semistable. This does not assert that a single model defines a globally semistable local system on all of X.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued with perfect residue; locally choose an isogeny Z_p-lattice. Semistability of a stalk is over its own residue field.
proofSteps: For the horizontal theorem localize R at the prime (π), complete to a discretely valued field with possibly imperfect residue, and use horizontal monodromy there. The canonical constant field is K. Descend semistability back by the purity theorem, Shimizu Theorem 6.1. The specialization test forces N=0 in the crystalline case. Around a classical point choose a polydisk and shrink it until the flat connection has a full set of solutions, by the convergent Taylor construction of Theorem 9.7. Apply the horizontal theorem. Compactness of the set of K-points gives the qc consequence.
acceptance: For a non-K-rational point the neighborhood lies after k(x)-base change.
The union of these neighborhoods need not contain every nonclassical point of X.

sources.locator: Theorems 6.1, 7.4–7.5, pp.34,44–45; Theorem 9.2, Remark 9.3, Corollary 9.4 and Theorem 9.7, pp.49–53
sources.match: Proves horizontal monodromy by purity and deduces the precise neighborhood and stalk assertions.

nodes.title: Small-weight ordinarity branches
nodes.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite unramified and V a two-dimensional continuous E-representation with a G_F-stable lattice lifting an ordinary residual representation. Use the weight-k convention V⊗_{E,ι}C_p≅C_p⊕C_p(k−1) for every ι. If V is crystalline and 2≤k≤p, it is ordinary: it has a stable E-line with unramified quotient and, on an open inertia subgroup, cyclotomic exponent k−1 on the line. When F=Q_p the same assertion holds for 2≤k≤p+1. Separately, every semistable noncrystalline weight-two V is ordinary. The third branch of Khare–Wintenberger Lemma 3.5 says that a weight-two lift crystalline over Q_p^nr(μ_p) is ordinary when its residual representation is ordinary. The branches retain their distinct integral inputs; the p+1 case is not deduced from the strict Fontaine–Laffaille interval.
hypotheses: E/Q_p finite; all lattice and residual hypotheses as stated. The convention gives positive Tate-module weights.
proofSteps: For 2≤k≤p import the strongly divisible-lattice subobject argument: the ordinary residual quotient produces a nonzero Fil^1=0 Frobenius-invertible subobject, including the special k=p argument. Apply the contravariant Fontaine–Laffaille functor to obtain an unramified quotient. At F=Q_p,k=p+1 use Berger–Li–Zhu’s reduction of crystalline two-dimensional representations and its valuation branches. For semistable noncrystalline weight two, Nφ=pφN forces slopes −1,0, and weak admissibility yields the unramified quotient. The potential-crystalline weight-two branch uses Conrad–Diamond–Taylor Lemma 2.1.2. In the last branch, use the Barsotti–Tate realization over a finite unramified extension of Q_p(μ_p), of absolute ramification index p−1. If its étale part vanished, a residual invariant gives a generic constant subgroup of Γ[p]. Its schematic closure is μ_p by the ramification-bound uniqueness theorem; Cartier duality then forces a nonzero étale quotient of the dual. The determinant gives the cyclotomic character on the connected factor and ranks one on both sides. Descent of this canonical connected–étale flag gives ordinarity.
acceptance: At p=2 the ordinary weight-two crystalline case still exists; an empty interval [0,p−2] is not its proof.
The endpoint p+1 is only asserted for F=Q_p.

sources.match: States the three ordinarity branches and identifies their separate integral proofs.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1.1, Remark 4.1.2, Corollary 4.1.3 and Proposition 4.1.4, pp.7–9
sources.match: Supplies crystalline reduction computations for the Q_p endpoint beyond Fontaine–Laffaille.

sources.locator: Lemma 2.1.2 and proof, author p.9 (published p.529)
sources.match: The connected–étale sequence and Cartier duality force the two ordinary rank-one factors.

nodes.title: Proper smooth de Rham representations
nodes.statement: Let K be complete discretely valued of mixed characteristic with perfect residue and X/K proper smooth rigid. For a de Rham lisse Q_p-sheaf L associated to (E,∇,Fil), H^i_et(X_C,L) is de Rham and D_dR(H^i_et(X_C,L))≅H^i_dR(X,E) with its Hodge filtration. The filtered G_K-equivariant B_dR comparison is compatible with cup products, duality, Tate twists and smooth proper base change. In particular the constant-coefficient representations are de Rham; their Hodge–Tate graded components are H^{i−j}(X,Ω_X^j) with twist −j. For nonconstant coefficients use the associated filtered de Rham complex, not the untwisted Hodge groups.
hypotheses: Proper smooth X and de Rham L; the Hodge filtration is the filtration of the de Rham complex with coefficients.

For trace and cycle classes use the P¹-normalized twist comparison a of Betts–Stix Proposition 3.20. Equality of a with the t-defined twist comparison requires a separate compatibility proof (Remark 3.21).
proofSteps: Use the early positive comparison and corrected local Poincaré resolution. Compare the filtered cohomology complexes, prove Hodge–de Rham degeneration using the period lattice, and take G_K-invariants in the resulting filtered comparison. Tensor and cup compatibility follow from the local resolutions; use proper base change for families.
acceptance: For P^1, H^2_et=Q_p(−1) has Hodge–Tate weight −1 and D_dR has jump +1.

sources.match: Establishes absolute and relative filtered comparisons directly from the local period sheaves.
Fixes the twist comparison used for traces and algebraic cycle classes and distinguishes it from the t-normalized candidate.

nodes.title: Proper smooth formal crystalline comparison
nodes.statement: Let K be complete discretely valued of mixed characteristic with perfect residue k, and 𝔛 a proper smooth p-adic formal O_K-scheme with rigid generic fiber X. For every i, the natural comparison H^i_et(X_C,Z_p)⊗_{Z_p}B_cris≅H^i_cris(𝔛_k/W(k))⊗_{W(k)}B_cris is an isomorphism compatible with G_K, Frobenius, cup products and, after the fixed B_cris→B_dR map, the filtration transported from H^i_dR(X/K). Consequently the rational étale cohomology is crystalline and its D_cris is H^i_cris[1/p]. No torsion-freeness hypothesis on integral crystalline cohomology is imposed on this rational comparison.
hypotheses: 𝔛 proper smooth formal, not an arbitrary rigid space with unverified reduction. Invert p in the crystalline cohomology where it is viewed as a filtered isocrystal.
proofSteps: Use the AI.5 A_inf comparison theorem for a proper smooth formal scheme and its crystalline specialization. Base change the complex along A_inf→B_cris using the derived crystalline base change of CR.3. Compare with the rational étale realization, and check the filtered B_dR compatibility through the proper-smooth de Rham comparison. This is BMS Theorem 14.6(i). Integral A_inf and Breuil–Kisin lattice recovery are supplied by AI.5 and R07.4.
acceptance: Torsion in H_cris disappears after B_cris extension; it does not invalidate this comparison.
For the Tate module of an abelian scheme dualize H^1_et before identifying D_cris.

sources.locator: Theorem 14.6(i) and proof, pp.121–122; Theorem 13.21, pp.116–117
sources.match: Provides the formal-model crystalline comparison and its filtered compatibility.

nodes.title: Semistable comparison from a logarithmic model
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛/O_K be a proper semistable scheme or proper semistable p-adic formal scheme, with its divisorial log structure, and smooth proper generic fiber X. The log special fiber gives a Hyodo–Kato K_0-complex with Frobenius φ and monodromy N satisfying Nφ=pφN. For a uniformizer π there is a G_K-equivariant comparison H^i_et(X_C,Q_p)⊗B_st≅H^i_HK(𝔛_k)⊗_{K_0}B_st, respecting φ, the diagonal N and cup products. After B_st→B_dR attached to π, it agrees with the filtered de Rham comparison through the Hyodo–Kato map ι_π. Thus H^i_et is semistable and D_st≅H^i_HK. Use CR.6’s uniformizer-indexed map and its change-of-uniformizer law in the convention Nφ=pφN; transport the B_st embedding by the same logarithm coordinate change. The comparison is compatible with this transport. Proper smooth reduction specializes to crystalline comparison with N=0.
hypotheses: The log structure and log base are part of the input. Finite-type and p-adic formal versions use their respective comparison theorem and proper formal GAGA.

For the scheme theorem the log scheme is proper, fine and saturated, log-smooth over O_K with the standard base log structure and has Cartier-type reduction. For the formal theorem use a proper semistable p-adic formal scheme. K is a finite extension of Q_p, as in the selected Colmez–Nizioł comparison theorem.
proofSteps: Use the logarithmic period complex and syntomic fiber below. For r>i, Corollary 5.12 (schemes) or 5.21 (formal schemes) identifies its cohomology with H^i_et(X_C,Q_p(r)). Project to (H^i_HK⊗B_st)^{φ=p^r,N=0}, then remove the Tate twist.

The syntomic presentation gives the long exact sequence of X_st^r and X_dR^r. Banach–Colmez dimension and height show equality of Hodge and Newton totals, bijectivity of the Hyodo–Kato-to-de Rham map and surjectivity onto the filtered quotient (Proposition 5.20). The kernel therefore has rank dim H_HK and reconstructs the admissible module.

For formal schemes use Proposition 5.22 with r>i; its inverse limits are controlled by early proper-smooth finiteness. Check φ,N,G_K and filtered compatibility on the defining diagrams before extending scalars. Multiplicativity is checked on the local Fontaine–Messing period map.
acceptance: The Tate curve model has N≠0 and is not assigned a crystalline comparison.
A choice of π gives an embedding, not an additional intrinsic G_K action on H_HK.

sources.locator: Corollaries 5.12 and 5.15, pp.59–60; Propositions 5.20 and 5.22, pp.62–65; Corollaries 5.21 and 5.26, pp.63,66
sources.match: Constructs the Fontaine–Messing period map and obtains the semistable comparison for schemes and formal models through the syntomic two-term presentation and Banach–Colmez dimension argument.
Fixes semistable log models and the Hyodo–Kato realization interface.

nodes.title: The first-order fundamental period diagram
nodes.statement: For a smooth rigid space X over complete algebraically closed C/Q_p, there is a natural commutative diagram of short exact pro-étale sheaf sequences: 0→Q_p(1)→(B_cris^+)^{φ=p}→Ô_X→0 and 0→Ô_X(1)→B_dR^+/t²→Ô_X→0. The right vertical map is the identity, the middle map is the period embedding followed by reduction modulo t², and the left map is the natural inclusion Q_p(1)→Ô_X(1). The top surjection is θ; the bottom is θ modulo t². The lower kernel is tB_dR^+/t², identified with Ô_X(1), not with the constant Q_p(1).
hypotheses: Period sheaves are shared with the corrected local-rational construction; exactness is in sheaves, not necessarily on every affinoid perfectoid section ring.
proofSteps: The lower row follows from gr^1 B_dR^+=Ô_X(1). Solve the φ=p lifting problem pro-étale locally for the top row by the crystalline fundamental-sequence construction. Multiplication by t identifies its kernel with the cyclotomic constant sheaf. Functoriality of θ and the period embedding makes the diagram commute.
acceptance: At Spa(C,O_C) the two left terms are Q_p(1) and C(1), respectively.
The natural cohomological boundary is used together with the intrinsic Kummer-to-dlog isomorphism; the rows alone do not compute curve cohomology.

sources.match: Uses precisely these two exact rows and their common right term for the canonical comparison diagram.

nodes.title: Logarithmic period complexes of semistable charts
nodes.statement: For a semistable chart R/O_K in Colmez–Nizioł §2.1, let S=R_π^PD be the logarithmic PD lift over the uniformizer variable, Λ=A_cris(Rbar), and ι:S→Λ the Kummer root embedding. Form the p-adically completed log-PD envelope E_R^PD of the multiplication map S⊗_{O_F}Λ→Λ, with partial PD level s=0 for p≥3 and s=1 for p=2. In logarithmic coordinates V_j=X_j/ι(X_j), sections have unique convergent expansions Σ_k a_k∏_j(1−V_j)^{[k_j]}, with a_k→0. The filtration is a_k∈Fil^{r−|k|}Λ, and the relative log connection is ∂_j=X_j∂/∂X_j. Frobenius and G_R act diagonally and extend continuously. The filtered log de Rham complex resolves Fil^rΛ after inverting p. This is a model-relative log-PD object; it is not a globally chosen polynomial OB_cris[u].
hypotheses: R has the semistable presentation of §2.1; use the source’s logarithmic base, p-adic completions and compatible Kummer roots. The PD lift and envelopes themselves are imported from CR.5–CR.6.
proofSteps: Apply the universal log-PD envelope to the chart map. Use the coefficient-extraction map and log derivations to prove uniqueness of the expansion, then lift from the étale toric chart to prove existence (Lemma 2.36). The source’s explicit contracting homotopy has denominators bounded by p^s; thus Lemma 2.37 is a p^s-quasi-isomorphism and becomes exact after inverting p. Extend φ and G_R by the formulas on the V_j and the PD universal property (Lemma 2.40).
acceptance: The logarithmic PD coordinate V_j−1 is present; replacing it by an ordinary polynomial variable gives the wrong integral ring.

sources.match: Defines the completed log-PD ring, expansion, filtration, contracting homotopy and operators; the point case is the completed semistable period ring.

tests.statement: A coefficient multiplying a PD monomial of total degree m lies in Fil^{r−m}Λ in filtration step r.

Gives an actual log-PD period evaluation for the model’s charts.

nodes.title: The rational semistable syntomic fiber
nodes.statement: For a proper semistable model 𝔛 and r≥0, define the rational geometric syntomic complex as the homotopy fiber of [RΓ_HK(𝔛_k)⊗B_st^+]^{φ=p^r,N=0}→(RΓ_dR(X)⊗B_dR^+)/Fil^r. Here the bracket is a derived joint invariant complex: the φ map in monodromy degree 0 is 1−p^{−r}φ and in monodromy degree 1 is 1−p^{1−r}φ; the vertical maps are N, so Nφ=pφN makes the square commute. Totalize the square and then take the fiber to the filtered de Rham quotient. The source’s log-crystalline syntomic complex identifies with this complex for schemes and proper semistable formal models with Cartier-type reduction. For r>i its H^i identifies with H^i_et(X_C,Q_p(r)) through Fontaine–Messing.
hypotheses: Use finite-dimensional HK complexes and the uniformizer-compatible filtered comparison from CR.6. The formula is derived; ordinary simultaneous fixed vectors are only used after the cohomology comparison theorem.
proofSteps: Construct the commuting Frobenius/monodromy square, then its total complex. Apply CR.6’s HK-to-log-crystalline identification and the log-PD Poincaré complex to identify the crystalline syntomic fiber. The filtered derived de Rham base change gives the quotient term. Apply the local Fontaine–Messing nearby-cycle map and proper descent, controlling inverse limits by primitive finiteness.
acceptance: Changing r changes both φ normalizations; using 1−p^{−r}φ on both rows fails to commute with N.

sources.locator: Equation (5.13), pp.59–60; Proposition 5.22, pp.64–65; Corollaries 5.12 and 5.21, pp.59,63
sources.match: Gives the derived invariant square, syntomic homotopy fiber and nearby-cycle identification in the stable degree range.

api.name: SemistableSyntomic.period

nodes.title: Perfect period rings over a perfect uniform algebra
nodes.statement: For a perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra R with an open integrally closed subring R^+, form W(R), W(R)[1/p] and W(R^+). For x=Σ_i p^i[x_i], use the Witt Gauss norms λ_r(x)=max_i p^{−i}α(x_i)^r. Define the integral radius-r ring by the condition lim_{i→∞}p^{−i}α(x_i)^r=0 on x=Σ_{i≥0}p^i[x_i]; the bounded radius-r ring inverts p with bounded Witt coefficients. Complete bounded rings for max(λ_s,λ_r) to obtain the closed-interval ring R̃_R^{[s,r]}, take the inverse limit over s↓0 for R̃_R^r, and the direct limit over r↓0 for the Robba ring R̃_R. The bounded and integral Robba rings are the corresponding radius unions. For R^+, every integral radius ring is W(R^+), every bounded radius ring is W(R^+)[1/p], and R̃_R^+ is its completion for all λ_s, s>0; this can be smaller than ⋂_{r>0}R̃_R^r. Retain the specified R^+ rather than recovering it from rank-one points. Frobenius sends radius r to r/p and respects the interval maps. At a perfect analytic field these are the existing extended Robba rings, not a second field construction.
hypotheses: α is the power-multiplicative spectral norm; R is complete and perfect, and the specified R^+ is part of the adic algebra. All Witt expansions and all radius completions are the precise ones of KL Definition 5.1.1.
R is an adic Banach algebra over a perfect analytic field, as in KL Hypothesis 5.0.1.
proofSteps: Extend the lower-stage field Witt-Gauss construction coefficientwise to R using Witt addition estimates. Prove the norm and completeness assertions, then the restriction maps for nested intervals. Use the rational-cover splitting argument of KL Lemma 5.3.2 to prove the sheaf and acyclicity statements only for the rings actually listed in Theorem 5.3.3. Positive variants have separate sheaf assertions and are not supplied the same acyclicity theorem.
acceptance: The integral-positive and positive variants are omitted from the ordinary acyclicity list.

sources.locator: Definition 5.1.1 and Lemma 5.1.2, pp.113–114; Definition 5.3.1 and Theorem 5.3.3, pp.121–122
sources.match: Specifies the relative Witt-Gauss rings, interval and radius limits, and the restricted rational acyclicity list.

Provides the period rings in which pure and étale loci are tested.

nodes.title: Relative Witt and Robba period sheaves
nodes.statement: Let X be a preadic space over Q_{p^d}, d≥1, with the KL pro-étale site. On a perfectoid subdomain Y let R=O(Y^flat) and R^+ its integral ring. Define Ã_X(Y)=W(R), Ã_X^+(Y)=W(R^+), B̃_X(Y)=W(R)[1/p], and the overconvergent integral, bounded and interval sheaves by the relative radius rings above: Ã_X^{†,r}=R̃_R^{int,r}, B̃_X^{†,r}=R̃_R^{bd,r}, C̃_X^I=R̃_R^I, with their radius limits Ã_X^†,B̃_X^†,C̃_X. Sheafify on the perfectoid basis. A φ^d-module is a finite locally projective module sheaf with an isomorphism φ^{d*}M≅M. Pure and étale mean those conditions on every geometric perfectoid evaluation; a lift-independent test suffices by pointwise slope theory. Integral-positive Witt sections have only almost acyclicity. Use ordinary acyclicity and unrestricted perfectoid evaluation only for the ring variants whose proof applies; no blanket acyclicity is imposed.
hypotheses: X and d satisfy KL Hypothesis 9.3.2; the positive and radius topologies are retained. This definition is independent of choosing a toric cover of X.
proofSteps: Apply the relative ring construction to the tilt on each perfectoid subdomain. Glue through the rational and pro-étale sheaf property. Transport Frobenius and finite projective modules through descent. For evaluation away from the basis, use the corrected cohomological restriction of Remark 9.3.17, not the false integral-positive clause of Lemma 9.3.4.
acceptance: A chosen free basis is unnecessary; finite locally projective sheaves are the objects.

sources.locator: Hypothesis 9.3.2, Definitions 9.3.3 and 9.3.5, Lemma 9.3.4, p.196; Remark 9.3.17, p.198
sources.match: Defines the perfect period sheaves, their φ-modules and perfectoid evaluation; the integral-positive acyclicity clause is corrected by the source issue.

Evaluates modules on perfectoid objects with the corrected acyclicity restrictions.

nodes.title: Pure and étale loci of relative Frobenius modules
nodes.statement: For a φ^d-module M over C̃_X, its pure locus and its étale locus are partially proper open subsets of X. If X is taut, each locus is taut. The notion is independent of the choice of perfectoid lift; the slope normalization for φ^d divides Newton valuations by d. Only the locus where the whole module is pure is asserted open; the individual slope filtration need not glue across a changing polygon.
hypotheses: X is preadic over Q_{p^d}; M is finite locally projective with invertible Frobenius linearization.
proofSteps: Localize on X=Spa(A,A^+), choose a perfectoid faithfully covering algebra as in KL Lemma 3.6.26, and apply the pure-locus theorem on its relative Robba ring. Descend the locus through the spectral map and use lift-independent pointwise slopes. Tautness follows from partially proper openness.
acceptance: A rank-one module φ^de=p^me has slope m/d; it is étale exactly when m=0.

sources.match: Proves partially proper openness after perfectoid localization and ensures pointwise slope tests are lift-independent.

nodes.title: Local systems and relative Frobenius modules
nodes.statement: For X preadic over Q_{p^d}, finite locally free étale Z_{p^d}-local systems are equivalent to φ^d-modules over Ã_X and over Ã_X^†. Rational Q_{p^d}-local systems are equivalent to étale φ^d-modules over B̃_X,B̃_X^† and C̃_X. The equivalences preserve rank, tensor products, duals and pullback. The inverse takes φ^d-fixed sections on sufficiently small pro-étale perfectoid objects; surjectivity of φ^d−1 is sheaf-local. Their curve realization is the pointwise degree-zero semistable vector-bundle category; its geometry and curve equivalence are supplied by the curve roadmap and are outgoing uses, not prerequisites of the local-system equivalence.
hypotheses: Finite projective φ-modules; the rational coefficient field is the unramified degree-d field Q_{p^d}. Retain étaleness on rational period modules; arbitrary φ-modules are not representations.
proofSteps: For the integral case apply perfect-field Artin–Schreier–Witt descent and the relative integral étale lattice theorem on each perfectoid basis object. Prove overconvergent extension is an equivalence and glue, using local-system descent. Invert p and use the pointwise slope-zero integral model to obtain the rational equivalences. Construct the inverse as locally constant fixed sections and prove the unit and counit locally before descent.
acceptance: For the unit rank-one module the inverse is the constant Z_{p^d} or Q_{p^d} local system.
A slope m/d line with m≠0 has no étale rational realization.
Rational étale realization must not require a global unit-root lattice: the local invariant sheaf construction accommodates KL Examples 8.5.17–8.5.18, pp.176–178.

sources.locator: Theorems 9.3.7 and 9.3.13 and proofs, pp.196–198; Theorems 8.5.5 and 8.5.12, pp.181–183
sources.match: Gives the integral and rational equivalences by localization of the perfectoid-base equivalences.

nodes.title: Relative Frobenius cohomology
nodes.statement: For a φ^d-module sheaf M define RΓ_{φ^d}(X,M) as the hypercohomology of [M→M], in degrees 0 and 1, with differential φ^d−1. For a local system T or V and the module realizations above, the natural maps identify pro-étale cohomology with this Frobenius cohomology over every integral or étale rational period variant. For a relative B-pair (M_e,M_dR^+,M_dR) with its two scalar-extension identifications, define RΓ_B as the hypercohomology of [M_e⊕M_dR^+→M_dR], (x,y)↦x−y. Once the relative B-pair equivalence supplies the same realization, the natural map identifies this cohomology with pro-étale cohomology. The B-pair is a sheaf pair with a common ambient module; it is not the quotient term of the fundamental period complex.
hypotheses: Use the integral or étale rational modules arising from a local system, not arbitrary positive sheaves. The relative B_e sheaf and period-patching equivalence are needed for the B-pair clause.
proofSteps: The sheaf exact sequence 0→T→M→M→0 follows from Artin–Schreier–Witt: the kernel is the fixed-section local system and φ^d−1 is made surjective by a pro-étale tower of finite étale covers. Compare the overconvergent sequence through its kernel and cokernel sheaves. Rationalize with the required limit control. The relative B-pair clause follows from the two-period-cover patching complex, whose derived identification must be established independently of blanket positive acyclicity.
acceptance: For a unit local system in degree zero, the kernel of φ^d−1 recovers its constant sections.

sources.locator: Definitions 9.4.1 and 9.4.4 and Theorems 9.4.2 and 9.4.5, pp.198–200
sources.match: Defines both two-term complexes and compares them with local-system cohomology via sheaf exactness and period patching.

nodes.title: Constructible primitive comparison with compact supports
nodes.statement: Let f:X→Y be a proper morphism of algebraic varieties over complete algebraically closed C/Q_p, let C^+⊆O_C be an open valuation subring, and let F be a constructible F_p-sheaf on X_et. On associated adic spaces the natural map (R^if_*F)^ad⊗O_Y^{+a}/p→R^if_*^ad(F^ad⊗O_X^{+a}/p) is an almost isomorphism for every i. In particular, for j:U↪X with X proper and F a finite locally constant Z/p^n-sheaf on U, H^i_et(X,j_!F)⊗O_C^a/p^n≅H^i_et(X^ad,j_!(F^ad⊗O_U^{+a}/p^n)); these groups on the left are finite. Naturality includes maps of pairs and finite coefficient change. X need not be smooth, so the statement applies to a singular minimal compactification once its algebraic model is supplied.
hypotheses: Constructibility and properness are essential. The p^n assertion follows by finite devissage from the F_p comparison; no unrestricted constructible Z_p assertion is included.
proofSteps: First prove the closed-immersion restriction formula for O^+/p. For a normal-crossings boundary, resolve j_!F_p by the alternating complex of its closed strata and apply smooth primitive comparison. Use characteristic-zero resolution and proper base change to replace a general compactification by that case. Trivialize a lisse F_p-sheaf after a finite étale torsor and use its normalized proper cover and Čech resolution. Induct on support dimension for constructible F. For the relative assertion check geometric stalks by proper base change. Devissage through multiplication by p proves the finite p^n form.
acceptance: For U=X and X smooth proper this is the earlier primitive comparison.
For an empty U both sides are zero; for a nonempty boundary j_! is retained and cannot be replaced by j_*.

sources.match: Derives constructible proper comparison by strata, resolution, finite covers and support induction.
Uses this extension-by-zero comparison on the proper minimal compactification.

nodes.title: Filtered derived completion for period comparisons
nodes.statement: Use decreasing sequences F^iA of complexes on a fixed small site, with gr^iA=Cone(F^{i+1}A→F^iA). Termwise quasi-isomorphisms define the filtered derived category; quasi-isomorphisms on gr define a distinct localization. If F^iA^n=0 for i≫0 in each degree and the filtration spectral sequence degenerates at E_1, all H^j(F^{i+1}A)→H^j(F^iA) are injective. If A→B is a graded quasi-isomorphism and A has these filtered cohomology objects, then B does too and the induced map on their filtration completions is an isomorphism. This does not assert an isomorphism on uncompleted cohomology.
hypotheses: Fix a κ-small basis/site within one universe. The degreewise boundedness is the hypothesis of the degeneration assertion; the comparison assertion assumes filtered cohomology. Completion is lim_i of finite filtration quotients with the required derived limit control.
proofSteps: Import the sequence and localization formalism from EnhancedDerivedSheaves. Identify gr by the displayed cone orientation. Degeneration kills the boundary maps in the long exact sequences and hence proves injectivity. Compare successive finite quotients by induction on the filtration interval, using Cone(F^k→F^j) for j≤k. Pass to inverse limits only after checking the R^1lim condition or using derived completion.
acceptance: An associated-graded isomorphism alone does not imply that an incomplete filtered object is unchanged.
The quotient F^j/F^k for j<k uses Cone(F^k→F^j), so reversal changes the cohomological shift.

sources.locator: Appendix A, Lemmas A.2–A.3 and Remarks A.1,A.4,A.5, pp.56–58
sources.match: Distinguishes the two localizations and proves the filtered-cohomology and completion assertions.

nodes.title: Derived pushforward of associated de Rham pairs
nodes.statement: For f:X→Y proper smooth between smooth rigid spaces over a finite extension K/Q_p and an associated pair (L,E,c) on X, form DR_{X/Y}(E)^n=Ω^n_{X/Y}⊗E with Fil^i term Ω^n⊗Fil^{i−n}E. Define H^i_dR(f,E)=R^if_*DR_{X/Y}(E), with filtration given by the images of R^if_*Fil^jDR. Its Gauss–Manin connection is the boundary of 0→f^{-1}Ω_Y^1⊗DR_{X/Y}(E)[−1]→DR_X(E)/σ^2→DR_{X/Y}(E)→0, where σ counts differentials from Y. Assume each R^if_*L is a lisse local system. The relative Poincaré map and the period projection map give the two filtered structural comparison maps; after filtration completion they are isomorphisms and recover a unique uncompleted associated de Rham pair. Hodge cohomology is locally free and the relative Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at E_1.
hypotheses: The filtered connection on E is integrable and Griffiths transverse; f is smooth proper and the source’s local-system assumption is kept explicitly. The structural OB_dR filtration is not assumed complete.
proofSteps: Construct the two relative de Rham complexes and their filtered comparison maps. On gradeds apply the proper-smooth period projection formula and the relative Poincaré lemma. Degeneration proves that the cohomology filtration is an actual filtration; apply the filtered completion theorem to the graded quasi-isomorphisms. Recover the associated pair using full faithfulness of completion on period local systems. Naturality of the σ-extension yields a flat connection, the Leibniz rule and Griffiths transversality.
acceptance: For the unit pair on a family of elliptic curves, the result has rank two, Fil^1=f_*Ω^1 and the Gauss–Manin connection.

sources.match: Constructs pushforward with Gauss–Manin, compares after completion and obtains degeneration and association.

nodes.title: Full faithfulness of structural period completion
nodes.statement: Let M_0,M_1 be filtered structural OB_dR-bundles with flat connection in the essential image of B_dR^+-local systems. Each filtered OB̂_dR-linear horizontal map M̂_0→M̂_1 is the completion of a unique filtered OB_dR-linear horizontal map M_0→M_1. The original map is invertible exactly when its completion is. The essential-image condition is part of the statement; this is not a completion theorem for arbitrary filtered OB_dR-bundles.
hypotheses: Completion is in the filtration, and the period local systems are finite locally free.
proofSteps: Apply the completed Poincaré lemma to identify Fil^0 horizontal sections of each completed bundle with its original B_dR^+-local system. Complete-period maps therefore restrict to maps of those local systems. Full faithfulness of the structural period functor reconstructs the original map; do the same for its inverse. Derived completion is controlled on perfectoid objects by graded Ô acyclicity and the inverse-limit lemma.
acceptance: For the trivial rank-one period local system, a completed horizontal filtered endomorphism is exactly its original B_dR^+-linear endomorphism.

sources.match: Proves full faithfulness and reflects isomorphisms on the indicated essential image.

nodes.title: Cup products, base change and analytification of de Rham pairs
nodes.statement: In the proper-smooth de Rham-pair setting with lisse higher direct images, a pairing of pairs induces the cup-product pairing of their direct-image pairs. Every commuting square with smooth proper vertical maps induces f^*R^iπ_*(L,E,c)→R^iπ′_*g^*(L,E,c); it is a morphism of filtered flat associated pairs, and is an isomorphism under the proper base-change hypotheses, in particular for a Cartesian square. For a smooth proper algebraic map of smooth K-varieties, analytification identifies filtered de Rham direct images and completed lisse étale direct images with their rigid counterparts. Consequently the absolute c_dR from this construction respects cup products, pullback, finite base extension and Künneth maps.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Q_p. Keep the completion on the Z_p-local system under analytification. Do not assert invertibility for a non-Cartesian commuting square.
proofSteps: Construct cup and base-change maps on the relative de Rham and local-system complexes. Naturality of the period projection and Poincaré maps makes the diagrams commute after completion; reflect them back using full faithfulness. Algebraic/analytic agreement uses coherent proper GAGA for de Rham complexes and the finite-coefficient étale comparison, then the controlled inverse limit for lisse Z_p. The Künneth compatibility follows from product projections and the cup-product identity.
acceptance: For f:X→point the product X×X comparison agrees with the exterior cup product.
The zero-to-nonzero map induced by a general non-Cartesian square need not be an isomorphism.

sources.match: Proves the pair compatibilities, algebraic/analytic agreement and formal compatibilities of the chosen absolute comparison.

nodes.title: Arithmetic Sen descent with analytic coefficients
nodes.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, E_∞=E(μ_{p^∞}), H_E=Gal(Ebar/E_∞), Γ_E=Gal(E_∞/E), and let F be a continuous semilinear coefficient sheaf satisfying the local orthonormalizability and strong decomposability hypotheses of arithmetic Sen theory. Define S_arit(F)=colim_{E′/E finite}(F^{H_{E′}})^{Γ_{E′}-an}. Its coefficient ring is the corresponding Galois-smooth, cyclotomically analytic subring. The normalized Lie derivative Θ=log(γ)/log χ_p(γ) is independent of sufficiently small γ and acts linearly over the Galois-smooth coefficient ring. Under the descent hypotheses the natural completed scalar extension from S_arit(F) recovers F, compatibly with continuous coefficient pullback, exact sequences admitted by the decompletion theorem and tensor operations. On finite-dimensional E-representations it specializes to Sen’s D_Sen and Θ. In the Hodge-type tower application, for coefficients annihilated by the horizontal u_P^0 action and satisfying the direct-summand orthonormalizable local models of BCGP 4.5.4, this gives the arithmetic descent and identifies Θ with the Hodge cocharacter action.
hypotheses: Strong decomposability, local continuous semilinear action, the normalized-trace estimates and orthonormalizable direct-summand models are hypotheses, rather than a theorem for every Banach sheaf. The u_P^0 and Hodge-type tower data are consumer hypotheses supplied outside this roadmap.
proofSteps: Apply the normalized-trace contraction to construct the cyclotomic decompletion after H_E-invariants. Use analytic vectors for the remaining one-dimensional Γ action and verify the normalized derivative on scalar coefficients. In the tower setting geometric Sen decompletion first kills the horizontal u_P^0 contribution and produces the finite-level Banach models; arithmetic Sen then decompletes the residual cyclotomic action. Identify the cocharacter operator on algebraic automorphic coefficient models, and extend through the given local completed bases.
acceptance: For Q_p(n), Θ=n; the sign is HT(χ_p)=+1.

sources.match: Specifies coefficient decompletion and arithmetic Sen for the local tower models; its geometric bundle functor remains at its owner.

nodes.title: Weight zero, unramifiedness and finite inertia
nodes.statement: For K/Q_p finite unramified and a finite-dimensional Q_p-representation V, V is crystalline with every Hodge–Tate weight zero if and only if inertia acts trivially. No semisimplicity is required. For an arbitrary finite K/Q_p, V is de Rham with all weights zero if and only if inertia has finite image; equivalently V becomes unramified after a finite extension. The coefficient-valued statements are obtained on the underlying Q_p-representation, retaining every labeled embedding weight.
hypotheses: Continuous finite-dimensional representations. In the first assertion K is unramified; in the second use potential semistability and all weights zero.
proofSteps: For the crystalline assertion, weak admissibility and zero filtration force slope zero, monodromy zero and a φ-stable lattice. Over Q_p the matrix is conjugate into GL_n(Z_p), giving a possibly nonsemisimple unramified representation. Reduce an unramified K to Q_p by unramified induction and use full faithfulness to restrict back. For the de Rham assertion apply the p-adic monodromy theorem, then the same zero-filtered weak-admissibility argument after the finite semistable extension. The reverse implication follows by finite de Rham descent from an unramified representation.
acceptance: A unipotent unramified Frobenius matrix [[1,1],[0,1]] is allowed.
A nontrivial finite ramified character has all weights zero and is de Rham but is not crystalline over its original field.

sources.locator: Proposition 8.3.5 and proof, pp.119–120; Proposition 9.3.1, p.146
sources.match: Classifies zero-filtered modules and gives unramified base change.
States the finite-inertia criterion attributed to Sen.

nodes.title: Berger’s Robba module of a filtered monodromy module
nodes.statement: For a filtered (φ,N)-module D over K, let 𝒟=(B_rig,K^†[ℓ_X]⊗_{K_0}D)^{N=0}, with the logarithmic monodromy normalization N(ℓ_X)=−p/(p−1). Transport the filtration on D_K to D_K^n by ξ_n induced by φ^n and the embedding ι_n=φ^{−n}, and set M_n=Fil^0(K_n((t))⊗_K D_K^n). The Frobenius-compatible lattices M_n determine the unique Robba lattice Δ(D) in 𝒟[1/t] whose K_n[[t]] localization is M_n for all sufficiently large n. For finite descent data construct over the semistable field and descend. Δ(D) has rank dim D, is an exact tensor functor on strict filtered sequences, and transforms the filtered-module HN degree t_H−t_N into the opposite Newton slope convention on Robba modules. In particular D is weakly admissible exactly when Δ(D) is étale. This gives an alternative proof route for admissibility after the étale representation realization; the independent Colmez–Fontaine proof remains earlier.
hypotheses: K/Q_p finite; φ invertible; N nilpotent; filtration exhaustive and separated. Strictness is required on filtered exact sequences. Use the corrected log variable normalization consistently.
proofSteps: Trivialize diagonal monodromy by a finite exponential in ℓ_X. Transport the filtration with φ^n so the local lattices are Frobenius compatible. Apply Berger’s lattice-gluing theorem: uniformly bound them between t^h𝒟 and t^{−h}𝒟, define the simultaneous localization intersection, prove finite freeness by the Robba Bézout theorem and interpolate one prescribed localization modulo t^h. Equality follows from local elementary divisors. Strict local exactness and tensor compatibility descend by uniqueness. Apply the HN comparison and relative slope-zero criterion for étaleness.
acceptance: For the unit D, Δ(D) is the unit Robba module.

sources.locator: Theorem II.1.2 and proof, pp.9–11; Definitions II.2.2–II.2.4 and Theorem II.2.6, pp.11–13; Theorem IV.2.1 and V.2.1, pp.19–22
sources.match: Glues the local filtration lattices and compares exact tensor and slope structures.
Recalls this construction and the weak-admissibility/étaleness dictionary.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic field of norms and Cohen periods
nodes.statement: For K/Q_p finite, K_n=K(μ_{p^n}) and K_∞=union K_n, the field of norms X_K has multiplicative carrier lim_N K_n. Multiplication is coordinatewise; addition at level n is lim_m N_{K_{n+m}/K_n}(x_{n+m}+y_{n+m}). It is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic p, identified with the field E_K inside C^flat by the p-power limit. Finite extensions L_∞/K_∞ correspond to finite separable extensions X_L/X_K; hence H_K is canonically G_{X_K}. Choose its Cohen lift A_K inside W(C^flat), with residue E_K, and put B_K=A_K[1/p]. Let B be the p-adic completion of the maximal unramified extension of B_K inside W(C^flat)[1/p], A=B∩W(C^flat). Then B^{H_K}=B_K, and φ and Γ_K act compatibly. The overconvergent rings are the intersections B^{†,r}=B∩B̃^{†,r}, with B_K^{†,r}=(B^{†,r})^{H_K}.
hypotheses: Use the eventually totally ramified cyclotomic tower and its actual residue field; its Γ_K action is the residual G_K/H_K action. Cohen parameters are choices, and their coordinate formula is asserted only in the unramified cyclotomic case.
proofSteps: Construct the norm-limit addition using ramification estimates, prove the valuation and completeness, and compare with the tilt limit. Prove finite-extension descent and construct the Cohen lift by unramified lifting, extending φ and the Galois action. Intersect with the weighted Witt overconvergence condition.
acceptance: For K unramified, X_K=k((ε−1)), π_K=[ε]−1 and φ(π_K)=(1+π_K)^p−1.

nodes.title: Frobenius and cyclotomic modules
nodes.statement: Over B_K, B_K^† or B_{rig,K}^†, a (φ,Γ_K)-module is a finite free module D with a semilinear Frobenius whose linearization R⊗_{φ,R}D→D is invertible and a continuous semilinear Γ_K-action commuting with φ. Over B_K or B_K^† it is étale when it admits an A_K or A_K^† lattice L with φ^*L=L. Over the Robba ring it is étale when it is obtained from such an étale overconvergent module; equivalently its Newton slopes are all zero. With E-coefficients use finite projective modules of fixed rank over E⊗R and check étaleness on every coefficient factor.
hypotheses: K,E/Q_p finite; Frobenius acts trivially on E. A φ-stable lattice is insufficient without the invertible integral linearization. The topology and semilinear scalar action are included in morphisms and continuity.
proofSteps: Use the shared Cohen and Robba carriers and their operators. Define the linearization and commuting action; define morphisms intertwining both. Construct tensor and dual operations by linearization. Import the Robba slope-zero criterion from RD.1.
acceptance: The unit object has the scalar φ and Γ actions and integral lattice A_K.

nodes.title: Étale realization and overconvergence
nodes.statement: The functors V↦D(V)=(B⊗V)^{H_K} and D↦(B⊗_{B_K}D)^{φ=1} are mutually inverse exact tensor equivalences between continuous finite-dimensional Q_p-representations of G_K and étale (φ,Γ_K)-modules over B_K. Every such D has a unique full-rank overconvergent realization D^† over B_K^†, with D=B_K⊗D^†. For every representation V, D^{†,r}(V)=(B^{†,r}⊗V)^{H_K} has rank dim V for sufficiently large r and D_rig^†(V)=B_rig,K^†⊗D^†(V). The equivalence extends to E-coefficients and to stable Z_p-lattices with integral étale modules. Overconvergence uses Γ_K and is not a theorem about arbitrary étale φ-modules.
hypotheses: K/Q_p finite. Integral descent uses finite free lattices and continuous action; rational coefficient extensions retain all factors.
proofSteps: Apply characteristic-p semilinear descent over the separable norm field and lift modulo p^n by Hensel and Hilbert 90. Take the complete limit and invert p; recover the residual Γ_K action. Apply the Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence theorem with its Tate–Sen estimates to obtain a finite-radius basis. Uniqueness follows from étale descent and the slope-zero full-faithfulness theorem.
acceptance: For Q_p(n) the basis has φ(e)=e, γ(e)=χ_p(γ)^n e; changing to t^{-n}e exposes the period Frobenius p^{-n}.

sources.match: Explains descent and states the representation and overconvergence equivalences.
Identifies the étale subcategory in the Robba realization.

nodes.title: Herr’s cyclotomic cohomology complex
nodes.statement: Let Δ_K be the finite torsion subgroup of Γ_K and choose γ generating Γ_K/Δ_K. For a rational coefficient (φ,Γ)-module put D′=D^{Δ_K}, using the average |Δ_K|^{-1}Σδ. Define C_{φ,γ}(D) in degrees 0,1,2 as D′→D′⊕D′→D′, with d^0(x)=((γ−1)x,(φ−1)x) and d^1(a,b)=(φ−1)a−(γ−1)b. Its cohomology is independent of the generator and compatible with finite extensions. For D_rig^†(V) it equals continuous G_K-cohomology. For any finite-free Robba module it is finite dimensional, has Euler characteristic −[K:Q_p]rank D, and cup product with D^∨(1) followed by the trace yields perfect local duality.
hypotheses: Rational coefficients allow the torsion average even for p=2. Integral p=2 complexes require a separate torsion-resolution interface and are not asserted by this formula.
proofSteps: Commutation proves d^1d^0=0. Identify H^0 with joint invariants and H^1 with extensions, and compare generators by the cyclotomic difference operators. Use the overconvergent-to-Robba cohomology comparison and Liu’s finiteness, Euler characteristic and duality theorems. Compare the étale case with Herr’s Galois complex, including its trace normalization.
acceptance: The signs and ordering of the two degree-one factors agree with Liu §2.1; swapping them requires changing d^1 and the cup formula.

nodes.title: Banach–Colmez period spaces
nodes.statement: Fix the category of sympathetic C-Banach algebras: spectral connected separable algebras Λ, with p-th power surjective on 1+Λ^{∘∘} and continuous C-point evaluations separating elements. A vector space is a functor on this category to Q_p-vector spaces, with exactness tested at every Λ. A Banach–Colmez space W has finite-dimensional Q_p-spaces V_1,V_2 and a common extension Y fitting exact sequences 0→V_1→Y→Λ^d→0 and 0→V_2→Y→W→0. Define Dim W=(d,dim_Qp V_1−dim_Qp V_2). Morphisms are morphisms of these period-space functors, rather than arbitrary maps of the Banach spaces W(C). The dimension-height pair is independent of presentation and additive on exact sequences; kernels and cokernels stay in this category.
hypotheses: Use a fixed universe and the evaluation-separated sympathetic category of Colmez–Nizioł §3.1.1. The chosen definition includes the separability needed for its analytic arguments.
proofSteps: Construct the functor category and constant Q_p and Λ-linear examples. Form finite-dimensional presentations and use the analytic dimension theorem to prove presentation independence. Descend kernels, images and cokernels through presentations to obtain the abelian category.
acceptance: Dimension and height depend on the period-space structure, although C and C⊕Q_p can be isomorphic as topological Q_p-spaces.

nodes.title: Almost C-representations
nodes.statement: For finite K/Q_p, an almost C-representation is a Q_p-Banach representation W of G_K for which there are finite-dimensional stable Q_p-subspaces V_2⊂W and V_1⊂C^d and a continuous equivariant isomorphism W/V_2≃C^d/V_1. Morphisms are continuous Q_p-linear G_K-equivariant maps. Its dimension is d and height dim V_2−dim V_1. This is an abelian category inside Banach representations with strict exactness, and dimension and height are additive. Finite-length B_dR^+-representations lie in it with dimension their length and height zero. The general-K definition exists, but the abelian-category and full-faithfulness theorems here require K/Q_p finite.
hypotheses: C is the completion of Kbar and actions on C are semilinear. Exact sequences use strict Banach maps.
proofSteps: Define almost isomorphism by finite-dimensional quotients, compare presentations using Banach–Colmez periods, and apply Fontaine’s abelian-category theorem. Use Sen theory to identify continuous equivariant maps between finite-length period representations with their B_dR^+-linear maps.
acceptance: A finite-dimensional Q_p-representation has dimension zero and height its Q_p-dimension.
