nodes.title: Wach and Kisin lattice comparison
nodes.statement: Let K=Frac W(k) be unramified, T a stable Z_p-lattice in a crystalline representation with HT weights in {0,…,r}, r≥0. Use the contravariant integral functors: M(T) is the Kisin module and N(T) the Wach module. Put R=O_C^flat, S_ε=W(k)[[v]]⊂W(R) via v=[ε]−1, and R̂=W(R)∩ℛ_{K_0}, where ℛ_{K_0} consists of the convergent sums Σ f_i t^{\{i\}}, f_i∈S[1/p], f_i→0, with t^{\{i\}}=t^i/(p^{q(i)}q(i)!) and i=(p−1)q(i)+s(i), 0≤s(i)<p−1. The (φ,Ĝ)-structure on M(T) gives a canonical isomorphism N(T)≃(R̂⊗_{φ,S}M(T))^{H_{p∞}}, H_{p∞}=Gal(Kbar/K(μ_{p∞})). It preserves φ and the residual Γ_K action. Inside T^∨⊗W(R), the Kisin and Wach realizations become equal after scalar extension to R̂. This is a comparison through R̂ and invariants; it does not assert equality of the two original modules over different scalar rings.
hypotheses: K unramified and T crystalline; both modules are attached by the same contravariant convention. The rational period comparison with covariant D_cris uses dualization. Any p=2 application uses the integral classification and the modified τ argument in Liu Lemma 3.3.2.
proofSteps: Compare the two bases through D_cris(T[1/p]) over ℛ_{K_0}. The Wach and Kisin realization inclusions bound denominators by powers of v and the corresponding I^[1] generator. Use the saturation statement of Liu Lemma 3.1.3, iterated on those powers, to prove that the change matrix and its inverse are in W(R), hence in R̂. Compute ℛ_{K_0}^{H_{p∞}} from the unique expansion and the nontrivial Kummer τ action; intersection with W(R) gives S_ε. Taking invariants of the equal realized submodules recovers N(T).
acceptance: For the trivial lattice both modules have rank one and the invariant comparison recovers the unit Wach module.
The cyclotomic twist must be dualized when passing from these contravariant lattice functors to the covariant period basis t^{-1}.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.0.2, p.2; §3.3, Theorem 3.3.1 and Lemma 3.3.2, pp.11–12; Lemma 3.1.3, p.9
sources.match: Gives the invariant formula and proves the change-matrix and invariant steps, isolating the integral saturation input.

nodes.title: Neighbouring representations and filtrations
nodes.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite, C=C_p, V a d-dimensional continuous Q_p-representation of G_K, M_1=B_dR^+⊗V, and M_2 a G_K-stable B_dR^+-lattice in B_dR⊗V. Call them neighbouring if both (M_1+M_2)/M_i have C-dimension one. In a Q_p-basis write the added line as C·t^{-1}α and the removed hyperplane as ker β, with Σ_iβ_iα_i=0. Put X=(B_e⊗V)∩(M_1+M_2) and let u_i:X→(M_1+M_2)/M_i be the quotient maps. If Σ_iβ_i⊗α_i is nonzero in C⊗_{Q_p}C, then u_2 is onto and V_2=ker u_2 is d-dimensional. If this tensor vanishes, Im u_2 has Q_p-dimension at most d and ker u_2 is infinite-dimensional. In the first case B_e⊗V_2≅B_e⊗V and B_dR⊗V_2≅B_dR⊗V, with positive lattices M_2 and M_1 respectively; V_2 is de Rham exactly when V is. For a filtered (φ,N)-module D, two filtrations with Σ_j dim_K((Fil_1^j+Fil_2^j)/(Fil_1^j∩Fil_2^j))=2 are neighbouring. Their positive period lattices are the corresponding neighbouring lattices, and admissibility is invariant under this modification.
hypotheses: Both one-dimensional quotient conditions are required. The scalar relation Σβ_iα_i=0 does not imply that the tensor Σβ_i⊗α_i vanishes.
The filtered-module clause uses the usual V_st construction and its induced lattice; all filtrations are finite and decreasing.
proofSteps: Apply the fundamental exact sequence to identify 0→V→X→C→0. The analytic fundamental lemma and its trace-kernel description determine the image of u_2 from the tensor Σβ_i⊗α_i.

In the nonzero case compare ranks and the two period trivializations. Recover the filtrations from the positive lattices to obtain the admissibility assertion. Irreducibility of V forces nonzero tensor: the minimal Q_p-subspace containing α is G_K-stable, so its coefficient coordinates are Q_p-independent.

The subcategory criterion used in the two applications is induction on dimension: require rank-one agreement, invariance along finite-dimensional neighbours, closure under extensions, preservation of the larger category from an irreducible neighbour, and a neighbour chain to the smaller category. These are hypotheses of the criterion; existence of a chain is proved in the application.
acceptance: The zero-tensor case must retain its infinite-dimensional kernel; it is not a second finite-dimensional representation.

sources.locator: Préface §2.2.2, Proposition 2.9, Remark 2.10 and note 18, pp.13–14; §2.2.3, p.14
sources.match: Describes the elementary lattice modification, its analytic dichotomy, the period identifications and the induction criterion.

nodes.title: Enhanced finite Frobenius–monodromy coefficients
nodes.statement: Let F=W(k)[1/p], k perfect. Let C_fin(F) be the abelian category of finite-dimensional F-vector spaces with invertible σ-semilinear φ and F-linear N satisfying Nφ=pφN. Define C_b(F) as the idempotent completion of its bounded dg-derived enhancement, and C_enh(F)=Ind(C_b(F)). The compact objects of C_enh(F) are exactly C_b(F). The intended geometric coefficient category over F^nr is the filtered colimit of these presentable categories under finite-unramified scalar extension, with its finite-dimensional bounded compact subcategory identified by descent. The proposed identification with an enhancement of C_fin(F^nr), and the factorization of Hyodo–Kato realization through it, require exact scalar extension and finite descent at the dg-derived level. The unrestricted derived category of all modules with endomorphisms φ,N is a different category and cannot supply the stated compact description.
hypotheses: Frobenius is invertible in C_fin. Finite-dimensionality is part of its carrier. Fix universes, dg enhancements and the variance of the realization before Ind-extension.
proofSteps: Construct C_fin and its exact scalar extension from the invertible Frobenius–monodromy category. Import bounded enhancements, idempotent completion and Ind from E0. Use the compact-object theorem for Ind of a small idempotent-complete stable category.

For the finite-unramified comparison descend the finitely many matrices of a bounded complex, its differentials and chain homotopies. Establish compatibility of the dg localization with this filtered scalar extension before identifying the colimit.

Check that the proper finite Hyodo–Kato realization has bounded finite-dimensional cohomology and invertible Frobenius, then choose its enhanced lift; the cohomological functor and a colimit-preserving homological extension have different variances.
acceptance: The finite isocrystal enhancement is specified explicitly; compactness of free modules in an unrestricted module category does not establish it.

sources.locator: Definition 3.1 and Remark 3.2, p.15; Definition 3.6 and Proposition 3.8, p.16

nodes.title: Relative two-period pairs
nodes.statement: For X preadic over Q_{p^d} and a perfectoid subdomain Y, let R_1,R_2,R_3 be the untilt-patching rings of AI.2. Set B_e,X(Y)=R_1, B_dR,X^+(Y)=R_2 and B_dR,X(Y)=R_3. Equivalently R_2 is the ker θ-adic completion of B̃_X^{†,1}(Y), and R_3 inverts a generator of this ideal. The untilt complement description identifies R_1 with the coordinate ring of the complement of its canonical untilt divisor. A relative B-pair is a triple of finite locally projective sheaves (M_e,M_dR^+,M_dR), with specified identifications M_e⊗_{B_e}B_dR≅M_dR≅M_dR^+⊗_{B_dR^+}B_dR. Morphisms respect both identifications. Finite-projective patching gives the period-pair realization of relative φ^d-modules; the vector-bundle realization on the relative curve is an outgoing interface owned by RF1/VB1.
hypotheses: X and d satisfy KL Hypothesis 9.3.2. The period-pair descent is the finite-projective untilt patching theorem; flat-coefficient cohomological exactness is stated separately.
proofSteps: Sheafify the three untilt-patching rings and glue the scalar-extension identifications. Identify the rational completion with the integral-radius completion through the fact that p is already a unit after θ-adic completion. Apply finite-projective triple descent from AI.2 locally and glue it along perfectoid covers.
acceptance: The two comparison maps are data. A pair with no common ambient identification is not an object of this category.

Integral local systems use integral Frobenius lattices; rational unit-root vector bundles require the local invariant sheaf realization and must not assume a global unit-root lattice, as shown by Examples 8.5.17–8.5.18. gaps.detail: Prove H^1(H_K,W(m_{C^flat}))=0 with continuous cochains and the p-adic topology, as used by Berger Lemma 2.27. proofDependencies.statement: Let O_C = 𝓞_ℂ_[p] be the valuation subring of C = ℂ_[p] (Mathlib PadicComplexInt). Then (i) p is not a unit of O_C; (ii) O_C is p-adically separated and complete, i.e. the instance IsAdicComplete (span {p}) O_C holds; (iii) the absolute Frobenius x ↦ x^p of O_C/pO_C is surjective. Consequently the Mathlib constructions fontaineTheta, PreTilt.untilt, fontaineThetaInvertP, BDeRhamPlus and BDeRham are defined for R = O_C, and θ: W(O_C^♭) → O_C is surjective by surjective_fontaineTheta.
hypotheses: p a prime; C = ℂ_[p] = completion of Q̄_p = PadicAlgCl p for the spectral norm, with |p| = 1/p (PadicComplex.valuation_p).
proofSteps: (i) v(p) = 1/p < 1 (PadicComplex.valuation_p), so p lies in the maximal ideal of the valuation ring O_C and is not a unit.

(ii) Since |p| < 1 and the value group of C is p^Q, the ideals p^n O_C are the closed balls {|x| ≤ p^{-n}}, so the p-adic topology of O_C is its norm topology. O_C is the closed unit ball of the complete field ℂ_[p] (a uniform-space completion, hence complete), so it is complete; it is separated because ⋂_n p^n O_C = {0}.
(iii) C is algebraically closed (PadicComplex.isAlgClosed), so every x ∈ O_C has a p-th root y ∈ C with |y| = |x|^{1/p} ≤ 1, i.e. y ∈ O_C; reducing modulo p gives surjectivity of Frobenius on O_C/p.
The three facts are exactly the instance arguments [Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R)], [IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R] of Mathlib's BDeRham file and the hypothesis hF of surjective_fontaineTheta.

proofDependencies.statement: (i) Let L/F be a Galois extension of fields (finite or infinite) and D a finite-dimensional L-vector space with a semilinear action of Gal(L/F) such that every vector has an open stabilizer. Then the natural map L ⊗_F D^{Gal(L/F)} → D is an isomorphism; equivalently H^1_cont(Gal(L/F), GL_n(L)) = 1 for L with the discrete topology. (ii) (Completed unramified descent.) Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field k, R' the completion of the maximal unramified extension R^{un} (residue field k̄), and M a finitely generated R'-module with a semilinear action of G_k = Gal(k̄/k) continuous for the natural topology of M. Then M^{G_k} is a finitely generated R-module and R' ⊗_R M^{G_k} → M is an isomorphism; after inverting a uniformiser, every finite-dimensional Frac(R')-vector space with continuous semilinear G_k-action is spanned by its invariants.
hypotheses: (i) needs only that the action is discrete (open stabilizers); no topology on F is used.
(ii) needs continuity of the G_k-action and completeness of R'; k perfect.
proofSteps: (i) Reduce to L/F finite: choose a basis of D and a finite Galois subextension L_1 fixing it (open stabilizers); D = L ⊗_{L_1} D_1 with D_1 the L_1-span of the basis.

(i) Finite case (Cartier's proof of Hilbert 90 for GL_n, F-O Theorem A.108(3)): for a cocycle c: Gal(L/F) → GL_n(L) put b(x) = Σ_σ c_σ σ(x) for x ∈ L^n; linear independence of characters (Dedekind) gives x with b(x) ... columns spanning, so b is invertible and c_σ = b σ(b)^{-1}. For n = 1 this is Mathlib's groupCohomology.isMulCoboundary₁_of_isMulCocycle₁_of_aut_to_units.

(ii) Reduce modulo the uniformiser π: M/πM is a finite-dimensional k̄-space with discrete semilinear G_k-action (continuity), so by (i) (M/πM)^{G_k} spans and H^1(G_k, M/πM) = 0 (as H^1(G_k, k̄) = 0 by the additive Hilbert 90).

(ii) Successive approximation with continuous 1-cocycles gives H^1_cont(G_k, Λ) = 0 for a G_k-stable lattice Λ, so Λ^{G_k}/π = (Λ/πΛ)^{G_k}; lift a k-basis to get an R-basis of Λ^{G_k} and conclude by Nakayama; torsion modules are handled by dévissage as in B-C Lemma 3.2.6.

proofDependencies.statement: Let A_inf = W(O_C^♭) and θ: A_inf → O_C Mathlib's fontaineTheta (surjective by R06.1/cp-integers-p-adically-complete). (1) ker θ = ξ A_inf with ξ = [p^♭] − p, and ξ differs by a unit of A_inf from AInfCohomology AI.0:integral's generator ξ_ε = μ/φ^{−1}(μ). The criterion used (an element w = (r_0, r_1, …) ∈ ker θ, in Witt coordinates, generates ker θ if and only if r_1 ∈ (O_C^♭)^×) and the fact that a generator is not a zero-divisor are the O_C instance of PerfectoidSpaces P1's primitive-kernel theorem; they are imported from AI.0:integral, which owns that instance under RS-01's owner record, and are not proved here. (2) θ is G_K-equivariant, W(k̄)-linear and open. (3) With θ_Q: A_inf[1/p] → C the p-inverted map (Mathlib fontaineThetaInvertP), ker θ_Q = ξ A_inf[1/p], A_inf ∩ (ker θ_Q)^j = (ker θ)^j for all j ≥ 1, and ⋂_j (ker θ_Q)^j = 0.

proofSteps: θ(ξ) = (p^♭)^♯ − p = 0. Since O_C has no p-torsion, ker θ ∩ p^n A_inf = p^n ker θ, and A_inf is p-adically complete, so it suffices that ker θ ⊆ (ξ, p) = ([p^♭], p): for w ∈ ker θ, v^♭(r_0) = v_p(r_0^♯) ≥ 1 = v^♭(p^♭) (B-C Proposition 4.4.3(1)). This special case is also given by PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel.

Apply AI.0:integral's imported criterion to the Witt coordinate r_1 (index 1) of [p^♭] − p; this coordinate equals −1. Thus [p^♭] − p generates ker θ. Since it and ξ_ε generate the same nonzero principal ideal in the domain A_inf, they differ by a unit. Here r_1 is a Witt coordinate, not a ghost component (B-C Proposition 4.4.3(2), pp. 58–59).
Openness and W(k̄)-linearity: B-C Proposition 4.4.2 (images of basic open ideals are open; θ([j(c)]) = h([c]) on Teichmüller digits). Equivariance: R06.1/galois-action-on-cp.

(3): A_inf/ker θ = O_C is p-torsion free, which gives A_inf ∩ ξA_inf[1/p] = ξA_inf and by induction the j-th powers; an element of ⋂(ker θ)^j has zeroth Witt coordinate r_0 divisible by all powers of p^♭, hence 0, so it lies in ⋂ p^n A_inf = 0 (B-C Corollary 4.4.5).

proofDependencies.statement: (1) There is a unique K_0-algebra embedding K̄ → B_dR^+ lifting the inclusion K̄ ⊆ C (composition with θ_dR is the identity), and it is G_K-equivariant; in particular B_dR^+ is a K-algebra and θ_dR is K-linear. proofDependencies.statement: The action of G_K on A_cris is continuous for the p-adic topology; equivalently, for every r ≥ 1 every element of A_cris/p^r has an open stabilizer in G_K.

It remains that A_cris/p^r is a W_r(O_C^♭/a)-algebra for an open ideal a of O_C^♭, since G_K acts discretely on O_C^♭/a. By Teichmüller expansions it suffices to take r = 1: ξ^p ∈ pA_cris gives [p^♭]^p ∈ pA_cris, so (p^♭)^p lies in the kernel of O_C^♭ → A_cris/p (B-C Proposition 9.1.2).

proofDependencies.statement: Let log: O_{K̄}^× → K̄ be the p-adic logarithm, trivial on roots of unity (Teichmüller lifts). For q ∈ m_K ∖ {0} and c ∈ K there is a unique homomorphism log_K: K̄^× → K̄ extending log with log_K(q) = c; it is G_K-equivariant, and changing c to c' changes log_K(x) by (v_p(x)/v_p(q))(c' − c). The standard (Iwasawa) choice is q = p, c = 0.

proofDependencies.statement: For f, g in O_K(I) and rho in I: |fg|_rho = |f|_rho |g|_rho, and for f, g nonzero n(fg, rho) = n(f, rho) + n(g, rho) and N(fg, rho) = N(f, rho) + N(g, rho). Consequently O_K(I) is an integral domain.

proofSteps: Let r = n(f, rho), s = n(g, rho). For the coefficient c_{r+s} of fg, the term a_r b_s has |a_r b_s| rho^{r+s} = |f|_rho |g|_rho, and every other term a_i b_{r+s-i} has i < r or r+s-i < s, hence strictly smaller size (Lazard, Proposition 1 proof).
The ultrametric inequality gives |c_n| rho^n <= |f|_rho |g|_rho for all n and strict inequality for n < r + s; so |fg|_rho = |f|_rho |g|_rho and n(fg, rho) = r + s. The statement for N is symmetric.

proofDependencies.statement: For f in O_K(I): (a) (three circles) for a, b in I and c in [0,1], with rho = a^c b^{1-c}, |f|_rho <= |f|_a^c |f|_b^{1-c}; equivalently log |f|_rho is a convex function of log rho on I; (b) hence for a closed interval [a,b] contained in I, sup_{rho in [a,b]} |f|_rho = max(|f|_a, |f|_b); (c) rho -> |f|_rho is continuous on I; (d) if f has no negative coefficients then rho -> |f|_rho is nondecreasing.

proofDependencies.statement: Let L be algebraically closed and complete over K, e in K, f in O_K(I), and rho in I cap |L^x|. Then sup {|ev_{e,z}(f)| : z in L, |z - e| = rho} = |f|_rho, and the supremum is attained. More precisely, if f != 0, there are finitely many residue discs D_1, ..., D_m of radius rho in the circle {|z - e| = rho} such that |ev_{e,z}(f)| = |f|_rho for every z on the circle outside D_1 cup ... cup D_m.

Rescaling: choose c in L with |c| = rho and a dominant index j; put g(w) = ev_{e, e + c w}(f) / (a_j c^j), a Laurent series over L in w converging on |w| = 1 with Gauss norm |g|_1 = 1 and coefficients tending to 0 in both directions.

k_L is algebraically closed, hence infinite; g-bar has finitely many zeros in k_L^x. For u in O_L^x whose residue u-bar is not a zero, |g(u)| = 1, i.e. |ev_{e, e+cu}(f)| = |f|_rho; the exceptional residue classes are the lifts of the zeros (Kedlaya overview Definition 3.2.1: the Gauss norm equals the spectral seminorm on the circle).

proofDependencies.statement: Let f in O_K(I) be nonzero. (a) For rho in I let n(f,rho) <= N(f,rho) be the least and greatest dominant indices. Both are nondecreasing functions of rho, and on every compact subinterval of I they take finitely many values. (b) The break radii {rho in I : n(f,rho) < N(f,rho)} form a discrete subset of I (finite in every compact subinterval). (c) On an open subinterval I' of I containing no break radius, n(f,.) = N(f,.) = j is constant, f = a_j T^j (1 + h) with h in O_K(I') and |h|_rho < 1 for all rho in I', and f is a unit of O_K(I') with inverse a_j^{-1} T^{-j} sum_{k>=0} (-h)^k. More generally f is a unit of O_K(J) for a compact interval J = [rho_1, rho_2] iff N(f, rho_1) = n(f, rho_2). (d) Hence if I has nonempty interior, f restricts to a unit on some nonempty open subinterval. (e) log |f|_rho is a piecewise affine function of log rho whose right (left) derivative at rho is N(f,rho) (n(f,rho)). (f) If L is algebraically closed and complete over K and ev_{e,z}(f) = 0 with |z - e| = rho in I, then rho is a break radius.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| (Kedlaya–Liu's 'analytic field'); O_K = {|x| <= 1}, m_K = {|x| < 1}, k = O_K/m_K. Characteristic 0 is assumed only where stated.
I is a nonempty interval contained in (0, +infinity): open, closed or half-open, possibly a single point, possibly unbounded above. The radius variable rho ranges over I.
proofSteps: (a) If n > N(f,rho) then |a_n| rho^n < |a_N| rho^N; multiplying by (rho'/rho)^n with rho' < rho shows n cannot become dominant at rho'; so dominant indices can only increase with rho. On a compact [rho_1, rho_2] the dominant indices lie between n(f, rho_1) and N(f, rho_2) (Lazard (1.8)).
(b) Between the finitely many candidate indices, each function log |a_n| + n log rho is affine in log rho, and the upper envelope of finitely many affine functions has finitely many corners.

(c) With a single dominant index j on I', h = (f - a_j T^j)/(a_j T^j) has |h|_rho < 1 for rho in I'; on each compact subinterval sup |h|_rho < 1 by continuity and compactness (gauss-norm-maximum-principle), so the geometric series converges in O_K(I') (frechet-topology). The closed-interval criterion is Lazard Proposition 4(1); necessity follows from additivity of n and N (gauss-norm-multiplicative).
(d) Take I' between two consecutive break radii inside the interior of I.
(e) On a break-free interval |f|_rho = |a_j| rho^j.
(f) If only one index j dominates at rho = |z - e| then |f(z) - a_j (z - e)^j| < |a_j| rho^j, so f(z) != 0.

proofDependencies.statement: Let f in O_K(I) be nonzero, rho in I, and s = N(f, rho) - n(f, rho). Then there is a unique polynomial P in K[T] of degree s with P(0) = 1 all of whose roots (in an algebraic closure, with the unique extended absolute value) have absolute value rho, and g in O_K({rho}) with a single dominant index n(f, rho) at rho (hence a unit of O_K({rho})), such that res f = P g in O_K({rho}). Consequently, for L algebraically closed and complete over K and e in K, f has exactly s zeros on the circle {z in L : |z - e| = rho} counted with multiplicity, finitely many zeros on each circle, and none on circles that are not break radii.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| (Kedlaya–Liu's 'analytic field'); O_K = {|x| <= 1}, m_K = {|x| < 1}, k = O_K/m_K. Characteristic 0 is assumed only where stated.
I is a nonempty interval contained in (0, +infinity): open, closed or half-open, possibly a single point, possibly unbounded above. The radius variable rho ranges over I.
The polynomial P is Lazard's m-extremal polynomial with m = -log rho.
proofSteps: Reduce to n(f,rho) = 0, N(f,rho) = s by multiplying by T^{-n(f,rho)}.

Hensel iteration in the Banach algebra O_K({rho}): start from P_1 = the dominant part sum_{0<=i<=s} a_i T^i; divide f = P_n g_n + Q_n with deg Q_n < s (division by an extremal polynomial, Lazard Lemme 2) and put P_{n+1} = P_n + Q_n; the corrections tend to 0 and the limits give f = P g (Lazard Proposition 2).
Uniqueness: Lazard Proposition 3.

Zeros: g has no zeros on the circle (newton-polygon-breaks (f)) and the zeros of P are its s roots of absolute value rho; zeros of f on the circle are those of P by multiplicativity of evaluation (evaluation-at-points).

sources.match: Existence and uniqueness of f = P g with P m-extremal of degree N - n and P(0) = 1.
On every closed disc f has the same zeros as a polynomial, with multiplicities.

proofDependencies.statement: Let alpha be algebraic over K with |alpha| in I (absolute value extended uniquely to K(alpha)), and let P in K[T] be its minimal polynomial. If f in O_K(I) satisfies ev_{0,alpha}(f) = 0, then f = P g for a unique g in O_K(I). More generally, if P in K[T] is separable, all its roots have absolute value in I, and f vanishes at every root of P, then P divides f in O_K(I).
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| (Kedlaya–Liu's 'analytic field'); O_K = {|x| <= 1}, m_K = {|x| < 1}, k = O_K/m_K. Characteristic 0 is assumed only where stated.
I is a nonempty interval contained in (0, +infinity): open, closed or half-open, possibly a single point, possibly unbounded above. The radius variable rho ranges over I.
Roots are taken in a finite Galois extension L of K, with the unique extension of the absolute value (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.2.1); separability is automatic in characteristic 0.
proofSteps: All conjugates beta of alpha have |beta| = |alpha| (uniqueness of the extension of the absolute value), and ev_{0,beta}(f) = tau(ev_{0,alpha}(f)) = 0 for the K-embedding tau with tau(alpha) = beta (evaluation-at-points, eval_map).

Division by T - beta over L: g_beta = sum_m b_m T^m with b_m = sum_{n > m} a_n beta^{n-1-m} for m >= 0 and b_m = -sum_{n <= m} a_n beta^{n-1-m} for m < 0; using sum_n a_n beta^n = 0 both formulas hold for all m, and choosing for each rho the formula whose terms are bounded by |a_n| rho^{n-1} (the first for rho >= |beta|, the second for rho <= |beta|) shows g_beta in O_L(I) and (T - beta) g_beta = f.
Iterate over the distinct roots (a root beta' != beta of P is a zero of g_beta since beta' - beta != 0 and O_L(I) -> L is a ring map).
Descent: the quotient f / P is fixed by Gal(L/K) acting on coefficients and unique (O_L(I) is a domain, gauss-norm-multiplicative), so it lies in O_K(I) (coefficient-extension).

sources.match: Divisibility by a polynomial is decided by the zeros; used for Q_n = phi^{n-1}(q).

proofDependencies.statement: If K is discretely valued with uniformiser pi_K and residue field k, then O_{E,K} is a complete discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal pi_K O_{E,K} and residue field k((T)), and E_K = O_{E,K}[1/pi_K] is its fraction field, a complete discretely valued field for |.|_1 with valuation ring O_{E,K}. No perfectness of k is needed.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| (Kedlaya–Liu's 'analytic field'); O_K = {|x| <= 1}, m_K = {|x| < 1}, k = O_K/m_K. Characteristic 0 is assumed only where stated.
K discretely valued with uniformiser pi_K; for K not discretely valued E_K is not a field in general (Kedlaya overview Remark 3.5.3).
proofSteps: Every nonzero f in E_K is pi_K^m u with |u|_1 = 1: the supremum of |a_n| is attained because |K^x| is discrete and a_n -> 0 at -infinity.

If |u|_1 = 1, the reduction of u in k((T)) is nonzero (amice-ring, reduction), hence a unit; lift its inverse to v in O_{E,K}; then uv = 1 - w with |w|_1 < 1, and sum_k w^k converges (amice-ring completeness), so u is a unit.
Hence O_{E,K} is local with maximal ideal pi_K O_{E,K}, noetherian of dimension one, i.e. a DVR, complete for |.|_1.

proofDependencies.statement: Let L be a complete valued extension of K (not necessarily finite) and I = [a, b] a compact interval in (0, infinity). Equip O_K(I) with |.|_I = max(|.|_a, |.|_b) and L with its absolute value. Then the natural map L tensor_K O_K(I) -> O_L(I) is an isometry for the product seminorm of Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.1.10 and extends to an isometric isomorphism L hat-tensor_K O_K(I) -> O_L(I). For an arbitrary interval I, O_L(I) = lim_J L hat-tensor_K O_K(J) over compact J contained in I.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| (Kedlaya–Liu's 'analytic field'); O_K = {|x| <= 1}, m_K = {|x| < 1}, k = O_K/m_K. Characteristic 0 is assumed only where stated.
L complete valued extension of K; I compact for the first statement.
proofSteps: Orthogonal basis: |sum a_n T^n|_I = sup_n |a_n| |T^n|_I with |T^n|_I = max(a^n, b^n) (gauss-norm; maximum principle).

Product seminorm: for x = sum_j mu_j tensor e_j with e_j = sum_n c_{jn} T^n, the coefficient lambda_n = sum_j mu_j c_{jn} of T^n satisfies |lambda_n| |T^n|_I <= max_j |mu_j| |e_j|_I, so the image norm is at most the product seminorm; the presentation x = sum lambda_n tensor T^n attains it. Hence the map is isometric (no spherical completeness needed).
Density: L[T, T^{-1}] is dense in O_L(I) (frechet-topology), so the completion maps onto O_L(I).
General I: annulus-limit-comparison (a).

proofDependencies.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, V an affinoid adic space smooth over Spa(K, O_K), x ∈ V and M = closure of {x} in V. Then there is a rational subset U ⊂ V containing M and an étale map U → Tⁿ = Spa(K⟨T₁^{±1}, …, Tₙ^{±1}⟩, O_K⟨T₁^{±1}, …, Tₙ^{±1}⟩) which factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps. Consequently every smooth adic space X over Spa(K, O_K) is covered by affinoid opens U with such toric charts, and these U can be chosen inside any given open neighbourhood of any point.
hypotheses: K complete nonarchimedean (any characteristic-0 field in the applications: k discretely valued, or a perfectoid K); V affinoid and smooth of pure dimension n over Spa(K, O_K).

Inputs from adic geometry (AdicEtaleGeometry A2): a smooth affinoid admits, after shrinking to a rational subset containing M, an étale map to the unit ball Bⁿ (Huber, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic varieties, Corollary 1.6.10, with the open set chosen to contain M); an étale map f: V → Bⁿ becomes, over a rational W ∋ f(x) and after restriction, an open embedding into a finite étale cover of W (Huber Lemma 2.2.8).
proofSteps: M is the intersection of the rational subsets containing it, so it suffices to produce the chart on some rational subset containing M.
Shrink V to a rational subset containing M with an étale f: V → Bⁿ (Huber 1.6.10, open set chosen to contain M).

With y = f(x) and N its closure, choose a rational W ⊂ Bⁿ containing N such that f^{-1}(W) → W factors as an open embedding f^{-1}(W) → Z followed by a finite étale Z → W (Huber 2.2.8); choose U ⊂ f^{-1}(W) containing M and rational in Z.
Embed Bⁿ into Tⁿ as the rational subset {|T_i − 1| ≤ |p|}; then U → W ⊂ Bⁿ ⊂ Tⁿ is a composite of rational embeddings and a finite étale map.

proofDependencies.statement: For X locally noetherian over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) and every U ∈ X_proét: (i) O_X^+(U) = {f ∈ O_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ |U|}; (ii) Ô_X^+(U) = {f ∈ Ô_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ |U|}. In particular Ô_X^+(U) is integrally closed in Ô_X(U), and f ∈ Ô_X^+(U) with |f(x)| ≤ |p|^n for all x lies in p^n Ô_X^+(U).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian over Spa(Q_p, Z_p); the statements are local in U, so U may be taken qcqs with a pro-étale presentation U = lim U_i (A1).
Imported from AI.3: O_X^+/p^n ≅ Ô_X^+/p^n (Lemma 4.2 (iii)).
proofSteps: (i): choose i with |U| → |U_i| surjective (possible for large i as transition maps are eventually surjective); if f = image of f_i ∈ O_X(U_i) has |f(x)| ≤ 1 everywhere then |f_i(x_i)| ≤ 1 on |U_i|, so f_i ∈ O^+_{X_ét}(U_i) by the corresponding property of affinoid adic spaces.

(ii): the inclusion ⊂ is by construction of the valuations. Conversely, as Ô_X(U) = Ô_X^+(U)[1/p], reduce to: f ∈ Ô_X^+(U) with |f(x)| ≤ |p|^n everywhere lies in p^n Ô_X^+(U). On a cover Ũ write f = f_0 + p^n g with f_0 ∈ O_X^+(Ũ), g ∈ Ô_X^+(Ũ) (Lemma 4.2 (iii), with g in the completed plus-ring); then |f_0| ≤ |p|^n, so f_0 ∈ p^n O_X^+(Ũ) by (i) applied to f_0/p^n; glue.
Integral closedness: an element integral over Ô_X^+(U) has |f(x)| ≤ 1 everywhere.

proofDependencies.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with open bounded valuation subring K^+, X locally noetherian over Spa(K, K^+), and U = lim U_i ∈ X_proét affinoid perfectoid with U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i^+) and Û = Spa(R, R^+) (AI.3). Let V_j = Spa(S_j, S_j^+) → U_j be étale and a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, and V = V_j ×_{U_j} U. Then V is affinoid perfectoid, V̂ = V_j ×_{U_j} Û, and Ô_X(V) = S_j ⊗̂_{R_j} R, the completion of S_j ⊗_{R_j} R for the topology in which the image of S_j^+ ⊗_{R_j^+} R^+ is open and bounded. The integral comparison A_j → Ô_X^+(V), with A_j the p-adic completion of the p-torsion-free quotient of S_j^+ ⊗_{R_j^+} R^+, is injective with cokernel killed by a power of p (by p^ε for every ε > 0 in log Γ after enlarging j).

This node records the rational consequence used by the period-sheaf computations (Lemma 6.18, Lemma 8.7 (i), the erratum's S_i).
proofSteps: By Lemma 4.5 (i)-(ii) (AI.3), V is affinoid perfectoid with V̂ = V_j ×_{U_j} Û, S = A_j[1/p], and coker(A_j → S^+) is killed by p^N.

Hence Ô_X^+(V) = S^+ (node completed-structure-sheaf-on-affinoid-perfectoids) and Ô_X(V) = S = A_j[1/p]; since A_j is the p-adic completion of the image of S_j^+ ⊗ R^+, A_j[1/p] is the completed tensor product S_j ⊗̂_{R_j} R.
Injectivity of A_j → S^+ holds because A_j is p-torsion free and the map becomes an isomorphism after inverting p.

proofDependencies.statement: Let X be locally noetherian over Spa(K, K^+), K perfectoid of characteristic 0, U ∈ X_proét affinoid perfectoid, S a profinite set and V = U × S (the pullback of S from the pro-finite-étale site of the base). Then V is affinoid perfectoid and F(V) = Hom_cont(S, F(U)) for F ∈ {Ô_X, B_inf, B_dR^+, B_dR, Fil^r B_dR^+, gr^i B_dR}, where Ô_X(U) has the p-adic topology of R, B_inf(U) the direct-limit topology, (B_inf/(ker θ)^n)(U) the quotient topology, B_dR^+(U) the inverse-limit topology and B_dR(U) the direct-limit topology. proofDependencies.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 and (R, R^+) a perfectoid affinoid (K, O_K)-algebra, and let θ': B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X_1, …, X_n]] → R be θ with X_i ↦ 0. Let S be a finitely generated O_k-algebra and f: S → B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X_1, …, X_n]] a ring homomorphism with θ'(f(S)) ⊂ R^+. Then f extends uniquely to a ring homomorphism from the p-adic completion Ŝ, continuous for the ker θ'-adic topology on the target modulo each power.
hypotheses: (R, R^+) perfectoid affinoid over (K, O_K) (the source's hypothesis K^+ = O_K); ξ as in R06.1 (Lemma 6.3) generates ker θ; gr^i B_dR^+(R, R^+) ≅ R (Corollary 6.4).
proofSteps: It suffices to extend modulo (ker θ')^i for every i, compatibly (then pass to the limit, B_dR^+[[X]] being ker θ'-adically complete).

With generators s_1, …, s_m of S: θ'(f(s_j)) ∈ R^+ = θ(W(R♭+)), so f(s_j) ∈ W(R♭+)[[X]] + ker θ'; hence the image of S modulo (ker θ')^i lies in the subalgebra (W(R♭+)[[X]]/(ker θ')^i)[ξ/p^k, X_1/p^k, …, X_n/p^k] for some k.

That subalgebra is p-adically complete: it is a finite successive extension of finitely generated R^+-submodules of the graded pieces gr^j ≅ R, and finitely generated R^+-submodules of R are p-adically complete (R^+ is p-adically complete and R^+ ⊂ R bounded). So f mod (ker θ')^i extends to Ŝ.

proofDependencies.statement: Let U = Spa(R, R^+) be an affinoid adic space of finite type over Spa(W(κ)[1/p], W(κ)) with an étale map U → Tⁿ. Then there is a finitely generated W(κ)[T_1^{±1}, …, T_n^{±1}]-algebra R_0^+ such that R_0 = R_0^+[1/p] is étale over W(κ)[1/p][T_1^{±1}, …, T_n^{±1}] and R^+ is the p-adic completion of R_0^+. proofDependencies.statement: In the situation of node local-structure-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf: (i) under OB_dR^+|_{X̃} ≅ B_dR^+|_{X̃}[[X_1, …, X_n]], ∇ corresponds to Σ_i ∂/∂X_i ⊗ dT_i, i.e. ∇(u_i) = dT_i ⊗ 1 and ∇ is B_dR^+-linear; (ii) Fil^r OB_dR^+ corresponds to (ξ, X_1, …, X_n)^r, with gr^r = ⊕_{a+|m|=r} Ô_X·ξ^a X^m; (iii) OB_dR|_{X̃} = B_dR^+[[X]][1/ξ], Fil^r OB_dR = Σ_j ξ^{-j}(ξ, X)^{r+j}, and OB_dR^+ ∩ Fil^r OB_dR = Fil^r OB_dR^+ for r ≥ 0.

(iii): since gr of B_dR^+[[X]] is the polynomial ring R[ξ, X] in which ξ is a nonzerodivisor, x ∈ B_dR^+[[X]] with ξ^j x ∈ (ξ, X)^{r+j} lies in (ξ, X)^r.

proofDependencies.statement: Let B be a Q-algebra and I = (ξ) + … an ideal-adic filtration on B[[X_1, …, X_n]] given by Fil^r = Σ_{a+|m|=r} Fil^a B · X^m for a complete separated decreasing filtration Fil^• B with ξ ∈ Fil¹B. Then the de Rham complex 0 → B → B[[X]] →d B[[X]] ⊗ Λ¹ → … → B[[X]] ⊗ Λⁿ → 0 (Λ^j free on dX_{i_1} ∧ … ∧ dX_{i_j}, d = Σ ∂/∂X_i dX_i) is exact, and it is strictly exact when Λ^j is placed in filtration degree j (i.e. the complex Fil^r B[[X]] → Fil^{r−1} ⊗ Λ¹ → … is exact for every r, and so is its associated graded).
hypotheses: B a Q-algebra (the applications: B = B_dR^+(R, R^+) with Fil = ξ-adic, and B = A_cris-type PD versions in the crystalline node).
proofSteps: Degree by degree in the monomial grading, the complex is the Koszul-type complex of the operators ∂/∂X_i, which on monomials multiply by exponents; over a Q-algebra the homotopy h(f dX_I) = Σ (integration in the first variable of I) gives exactness in positive degrees and kernel B in degree 0.

The homotopy preserves the filtration after the shift by one (integration raises the X-degree by 1 while dX_i has filtration degree 1), so each Fil^r-subcomplex and the graded complex are exact: strictness.

proofDependencies.statement: In the situation of node local-structure-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf, for every i ∈ Z there is an isomorphism of sheaves on X_proét/X̃_K, gr^i OB_dR ≅ ξ^i·Ô_X[X_1/ξ, …, X_n/ξ]; hence gr^• OB_dR ≅ Ô_X[ξ^{±1}, X_1, …, X_n] with ξ and all X_i in degree 1. Completed tensor with R of the splitting K = k_n ⊕ X_n gives R ⊗̂ K = R ⊗ k_n ⊕ R ⊗̂ X_n (R-linear, Γ-equivariant, bounded), and γ − χ(γ)^{-i} stays bijective with bounded inverse on R ⊗̂ X_n (the bounded inverse extends to completed tensor products); so H^q(Γ_n, R ⊗̂ X_n(i)) = 0 for all q (cohomology of Z_p on a module where γ − 1 is invertible).

On R ⊗ k_n(i) = R(i) ⊗ k_n: H^0 = ker(χ(γ)^i − 1), H^1 = coker(χ(γ)^i − 1); for i ≠ 0, χ(γ)^i − 1 ≠ 0 is invertible in Q_p, so both vanish; for i = 0, H^0 = H^1 = R ⊗ k_n and taking Gal(k_n/k)-invariants gives R; H^q = 0 for q ≥ 2 (cohomological dimension 1 of Z_p on Q-vector spaces).

For F ∈ B†,r_rig,K write F/∂(π_K) = Σ a_nπ_K^n; then F = ∂(Σ_{n≠−1} a_nπ_K^{n+1}/(n+1) + a_{−1}log π_K), the series converging on every smaller annulus (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/log-robba-ring-antiderivative in the variable u = π_K).

Induction on the log-degree using ∂(G_j log^j π_K) = ∂(G_j) log^j π_K + j G_j log^{j−1}(π_K) ∂(π_K)/π_K gives (2); the kernel statement (3) is the kernel statement of RD.2/log-robba-ring-antiderivative (constants K' = F'_K).
(4) (Berger Remark 4.5): the division by n + 1 shrinks the radius of convergence only by a factor tending to 1.

proofDependencies.statement: Let M be a free B^dagger_{rig,K}-module of rank d with a connection nabla_M over nabla. Such M (a 'cristal') is called unipotent; it is trivial if one can take nabla_M(f_i) = 0.

(2) => (1): induction on d; given e'_i with nabla_M(e'_i) = alpha_i f_0 and alpha_i in t B^dagger_{log,K}, solve nabla(beta_i) = alpha_i using the surjectivity of partial on B^dagger_{log,K} (P7/nabla-operator-on-robba-ring) and put e_i = e'_i - beta_i f_0.

proofDependencies.statement: Throughout: p is a prime, K a finite extension of Q_p with residue field k, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K_n = K(μ_{p^n}), K_∞ = ∪K_n, H_K = Gal(K̄/K_∞), Γ_K = G_K/H_K identified with an open subgroup of Z_p^× by χ, F'_K = K_∞ ∩ K_0^nr (the maximal unramified extension of K_0 in K_∞), r_n = p^{n−1}(p−1), n(r) the least n with r ≤ r_n, π = [ε] − 1 ∈ A_inf, q = φ(π)/π, π̄ = ε − 1 ∈ O_{C^♭}, t = log(1+π) = log[ε]. For w in the Weil group W_K let α(w) ∈ Z be defined by: the image of w in Gal(k̄/F_p) is the α(w)-th power of the absolute arithmetic Frobenius x ↦ x^p (so α(W_K) = f_K·Z with q_K = p^{f_K}, and α(Φ) = f_K for an arithmetic Frobenius lift Φ). A Weil–Deligne representation over a field Ω of characteristic 0 is a pair (r, N) with r: W_K → GL(D) of open kernel on I_K and N nilpotent with r(w)Nr(w)^{−1} = p^{α(w)}N, i.e. r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{−1} = q_K·N for arithmetic Φ (Deligne 8.4.1, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2). (a) For a (φ,N,Gal(L/K))-module D over E and embeddings τ, τ': L_0 → E, WD_τ(D) ≅ WD_{τ'}(D). (b) If V|_{G_L} is semistable and L ⊂ L' (both finite Galois over K), then WD(D_st,L'(V)) ≅ WD(D_st,L(V)).
hypotheses: Isomorphism classes only; the isomorphism in (a) is not canonical (it involves a power of φ and a rescaling of N).
proofSteps: (a): φ maps D_τ E-linearly and bijectively onto D_{τ∘σ^{−1}} (φ is σ-semilinear); it commutes with each r_D(w) (φ commutes with w̄ and with φ^{−α(w)}) and satisfies φ∘N = p^{−1}N∘φ, so φ: (D_τ, r, N) ≅ (D_{τσ^{−1}}, r, p^{−1}N). Every embedding is τ∘σ^{−j}.

A Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) is isomorphic to (r, aN) for every a ∈ E^× (Deligne's argument in Lemme 8.4.3, via the generalised eigenspaces of r(Φ): N maps the λ-eigenspace to the q^{−1}λ-eigenspace; supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2); hence WD_τ(D) ≅ WD_{τ'}(D).

(b): D_st,L'(V) = L'_0 ⊗_{L_0} D_st,L(V) compatibly with φ, N and Gal(L'/K) → Gal(L/K) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/potentially-semistable-dieudonne-module); for τ': L'_0 → E extending τ, the τ'-component of L'_0 ⊗_{L_0} D is D_τ, and r_{D'}(w) restricts to r_D(w) (same α(w)).

proofDependencies.statement: Let K = K_0 = W(k)[1/p] be absolutely unramified (e = 1), σ its Frobenius. A filtered φ-module D over K is weakly admissible in the sense of R06.2/weak-admissibility; its jumps are the i with gr^i D ≠ 0. For Fontaine–Laffaille (FL) objects we use the notation of FL 1982: MF_tor^{f,p} (finite-length W(k)-modules M with M^0 = M, M^p = 0 and φ^i: M^i → M), strongly divisible lattices (FL 7.7), the ring Ŝ and Ŝ_K = K ⊗ Ŝ, and the contravariant functors U_S(M) = Hom_{MF}(M, Ŝ) (lattices), U_S(M) = Ext^1(M, S) (torsion) and U_{S_K}(Δ) = Hom_{MF_K}(Δ, Ŝ_K) (rational), all supplied by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. Let D be a weakly admissible filtered φ-module over K with jumps in [a, b], and V := V_cris(D) the crystalline representation with D_cris(V) = D (covariant; R06.2). Then: (1) HT(V) = {−i : gr^iD ≠ 0} ⊂ [−b, −a]; (2) FL's contravariant U_{S_K}(D) ≅ V^* has HT(U_{S_K}(D)) = {i : gr^iD ≠ 0} ⊂ [a, b], with multiplicities dim gr^i D; (3) for a strongly divisible lattice M with jumps in [0, p−2], the contravariant lattice U_S(M) has HT weights in [0, p−2] (FL index i ↔ weight +i), and the covariant lattice U_S(M)^∨ = Hom_{Z_p}(U_S(M), Z_p) ⊂ V_cris(M[1/p]) has HT weights in [−(p−2), 0] (index i ↔ weight −i); (4) common Tate shift: if V has HT weights in [c, c + p − 2], then V(−c) has HT weights in [0, p − 2] and its contravariant module D*_cris(V(−c)) = D_cris(V(−c))^∨ has FL indices in [0, p − 2]; so every statement for the interval [0, p − 2] applies to [c, c + p − 2] after the twist T ↦ T(−c), which lowers every FL index of the contravariant module by c; (5) on rank one: U_S(M(1; n)) ≅ F_p(ω^n) (ω the mod p cyclotomic character) for 0 ≤ n ≤ p − 1, consistent with (2): Hodge–Tate weight n ↔ ω^n.
hypotheses: FL work with contravariant functors throughout (U_S, U_{S_K}, V_B^*); this node fixes the translation used by every R06.4 statement.
proofSteps: (1): D_dR(V) = D_K (K = K_0) with its filtration, and HT weights are the negatives of the jumps (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention).
(2): U_{S_K}(D) ≅ V_B(D)^* = V^* (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison) and HT(V^*) = −HT(V).
(3): U_S(M)[1/p] = U_{S_K}(M[1/p]) (FL 7.14–7.17, R07.3) and (2); duals negate weights.
(4): D_cris(V(−c)) = D_cris(V) ⊗ D_cris(Q_p(−c)) and D_cris(Q_p(−c)) has its jump at c, so the jumps of D_cris move from [−c−p+2, −c] to [−(p−2), 0]; dualising gives FL indices in [0, p−2].
(5): FL Théorème 5.3(iii) with h = 1 (R07.3): G acts on U_S(M(1; i_0)) by χ_1^{i_0}, χ_1 = ω for E = Q_p.

proofDependencies.statement: Let K = K_0 = W(k)[1/p] be absolutely unramified (e = 1), σ its Frobenius. A filtered φ-module D over K is weakly admissible in the sense of R06.2/weak-admissibility; its jumps are the i with gr^i D ≠ 0. For Fontaine–Laffaille (FL) objects we use the notation of FL 1982: MF_tor^{f,p} (finite-length W(k)-modules M with M^0 = M, M^p = 0 and φ^i: M^i → M), strongly divisible lattices (FL 7.7), the ring Ŝ and Ŝ_K = K ⊗ Ŝ, and the contravariant functors U_S(M) = Hom_{MF}(M, Ŝ) (lattices), U_S(M) = Ext^1(M, S) (torsion) and U_{S_K}(Δ) = Hom_{MF_K}(Δ, Ŝ_K) (rational), all supplied by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. For every prime p, let M(1; 0) and M(1; p−1) be the simple objects of MF_tor^{f,p} of rank one over k with jump 0, resp. p − 1 (FL §0.7). Then U_S(M(1; 0)) ≅ U_S(M(1; p−1)) ≅ F_p with trivial G_K-action, but Hom_{MF}(M(1; 0), M(1; p−1)) = 0 = Hom_{MF}(M(1; p−1), M(1; 0)); so U_S is not full on MF_tor^{f,p}. Rationally/integrally: Z_p (weight 0) and Z_p(p−1) (weight p−1) are lattices in the non-isomorphic crystalline characters Q_p and Q_p(p−1) with isomorphic reductions F_p = F_p(ω^{p−1}). At weight p (jumps {0, p}), Fontaine–Laffaille theory does not apply at all (Fil^p ≠ 0) and the Breuil–Kisin branch is needed (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/weight-p-plus-one-branch).
hypotheses: This is the only failure (FL §0.9: 'Mais c'est le seul ennui'); it is why the unrestricted torsion interval is [0, p−2].
proofSteps: U_S on rank-one simple objects: FL Théorème 5.3(iii) with h = 1 gives the character ω^{i_0}; ω^{p−1} = 1 (PARI/GP; Mathlib ZMod.units_pow_card_sub_one_eq_one).
No map M(1; 0) → M(1; p−1): on M(1; p−1) (killed by p) φ^0 = p^{p−1}φ^{p−1} = 0, while φ^0 is bijective on M(1; 0); compatibility f∘φ^0 = φ^0∘f forces f = 0.
No map M(1; p−1) → M(1; 0): f must map Fil^{p−1}M(1; p−1) = M(1; p−1) into Fil^{p−1}M(1; 0) = 0.
Hence U_S is not full; FL §0.9 identifies exactly this collision.
